nodes.title: {{Todd}}’s bedroom: a magazine and the TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, back in the upstairs hallway; the rooms are done. {{Todd}}’s bedroom door is open. A magazine lies on the cupboard by the door, and the small TV in the room can be switched on.

media.title: All Sports: Android QB
facts: All Sports reports that {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a “technical demo” android quarterback that can throw from end zone to end zone, hit a target six inches wide and run over 1,500 plays. American football has so far stayed human; the founder of an anti-android fan group says {{CyberLife}} hopes “to distort our sport the same way they have all the others.”

media.title: Tech Addict: The Price of Life
facts: Tech Addict explains how driverless cars choose whom to hit: the car’s imaging reads a pedestrian’s age, gender and life expectancy, public records add marital status, employment record and whether they have children, and each possible victim gets a “value”, with “a premium on lives that will save other lives, like doctors and nurses.” A critic answers that a criminal record does not make anyone less valuable: “That kind of information is irrelevant to the sanctity of human life.”

media.title: the TV in {{Todd}}’s bedroom
facts: On the sports news, the league is negotiating whether to allow one android player per basketball squad, and {{CyberLife}} has offered one specialized model to every team; androids already train players and advise coaches, but none has been allowed to compete.
The news: another 225,000 jobs were lost from the US economy in October, bringing unemployment up to 37.3%.

The news: President {{Warren}} opened a new {{CyberLife}} plant near Milwaukee, praised {{CyberLife}}’s role in the economy, and announced that the Department of Defense will acquire 200,000 android combat units.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “ANDROID QB” and READ “PUTTING A PRICE” (the chart’s label for the article “The Price of Life”): one magazine on the cupboard by the door of {{Todd}}’s room, with two covers. With them, the bedroom TV, which is not a chart node: Channel 16 sports, an animated film, CTN’s job figures, a hockey game and KNC on the President; the film and the hockey are left out. In the game both are available while cleaning his room and again after the talk with {{Alice}} (the transcript’s “Back In Hallway”); here they come after the talk. Facts are summarized from the transcript; presenters and interviewees are not named. No public-opinion effect (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). Dropped from the earlier R04: the stock market “up 11 percent” and “New Orleans may be underwater by 2055”, for which no source in this chapter exists.

nodes.title: Finished cleaning
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Your chores are done, and you go back downstairs. {{Alice}} sits at the dining table playing with her toy fox. {{Todd}}: “What are you doing?” {{Alice}}, nervously: “I… I’m playing…” “You’re playing…” He walks around the table. “I know what you’re thinking… You think your dad’s a lowlife… Huh? Fuckin’ loser? Can’t get a job, take care of his family? Don’t you think I tried to make things work!? But whatever I do when someone comes along, they just FUCK IT ALL UP!” He throws a chair aside. “I know what you think of me… You hate me… You hate me don’t ya?” He kicks a chair and grabs {{Alice}}. “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!” {{Alice}} cries. He puts her down. “God… What am I doing? I’m sorry, honey, I’m sorry…” He hugs her, crying. “You know I love you, don’t you? You know I love you…” Over his shoulder, {{Alice}} looks at you.

situationWhen.text: The table where she sits is clear; you washed the dishes earlier.
The dirty dishes and the magazine are still on the table where she sits.

facts: {{Todd}} raged at {{Alice}} at the dining table, threw a chair, grabbed her and shouted “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!”, then broke down, apologized and hugged her: “You know I love you, don’t you?”

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} watches, concerned.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending FINISHED CLEANING, reached on every path (the wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”). Every line is the transcript’s; the table is clear or still holds the dishes and the magazine, depending on WASH DISHES (cosmetic in the game). No stat change.

nodes.title: Welcome home
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, an android, caretaker and companion to {{Carl}}, the elderly painter whose paints you have just collected. It is November 5th, 2038, just before ten in the morning. The bus drops you in your neighborhood and you walk up to {{Carl}}’s house with the package. At the door: “Alarm deactivated. Welcome home, {{Markus}}.” The door opens by itself and you step inside. You set the package down on the hutch in the hall and hang up your coat. Your next task is to take care of {{Carl}}, who is still asleep upstairs.

situationWhen.text: In the hall mirror you see your shirt, torn where the protesters grabbed you.

facts: You came home to {{Carl}}’s house with his paints and left them on the hutch in the hall.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has delivered the package. The house is quiet; {{Carl}} is still asleep upstairs.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVING HOME and the next main-line node DROP OFF PACKAGE (the game’s objective DEPOSIT PACKAGE), narrated as one event. The alarm line is the template’s; the date and time (NOV 5TH, 2038, AM 09:58), the self-opening door, the hutch and the coat are the wiki transcript’s (“Markus places the package on hutch and hangs up his coat”). The mirror sentence appears only when the protesters tore his clothes in Shades of Color (`clothesTorn`), as the transcript’s mirror text changes (“his torn shirt” / “his unscathed shirt”). Left out: the optional looks at the mirror and at the painting behind the bench, which are not chart nodes. No stat change: the template has no arrow anywhere in the chapter, and the wiki gives no relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it (Markus has no Carl relationship stat).

nodes.title: The magazine in the living room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in {{Carl}}’s house before waking him. On the table in front of the living-room television lies a magazine with two covers.

media.title: Century: The North Pole - Why Russia Wants It
facts: Century (cover: “Frozen treasures”; also “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?”) reports that Russia’s interest in the North Pole has intensified since precious minerals used in synthesizing thirium were found trapped in the ice; surplus reserves would let either the US or Russia build more advanced androids and greatly boost its military and industrial output. NATO says “A conflict would benefit nobody”; President {{Warren}}: “It’s simple. Russia has no business in the Arctic. If the Kremlin doesn’t understand that, we will make them understand.”

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Life Found on Titan!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today (cover: “Life Found on Titan!”; also “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”) reports that a probe launched nineteen years ago has confirmed microorganisms living hundreds of kilometers below Titan’s surface, in a salt-water ocean under thick ice; after similar finds on Enceladus, life may be common in the universe. NASA calls its android expedition to Io one of many voyages seeking extraterrestrial life, and {{CyberLife}} says its space-faring androids are specially designed for long-range missions of this kind.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional side nodes READ “NORTH POLE RUSSIA” and READ “LIFE ON TITAN”: one magazine on the living-room table in front of the TV with two covers (the transcript’s “Read Magazine” with two tabs; BOOKWORM No. 2 and No. 27), drawn on the chart with no line to the main path. In the game it can be read from arrival until the pastime is chosen; here it is offered now, and whatever is left unread is offered again with the TV after breakfast (R05b). Facts are summarized from the article text in the transcript; interviewees are not named. No public-opinion effect: the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter, and the earlier version’s note that news can lower opinion is dropped. Titles corrected to the magazine’s own (“The North Pole - Why Russia Wants It”, “Life Found on Titan!”).

nodes.title: Waking {{Carl}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Upstairs, {{Carl}} is asleep in his bed, snoring. You draw the curtains; he wakes, shielding his eyes. “Good morning, {{Carl}}.” “Good morning.” “It’s 10 AM. The weather’s partly cloudy, 54°, 80% humidity, with a strong possibility of afternoon showers.” “It sounds like a good day to spend in bed…” “I did go to pick up the paint that you ordered.” “Oh yes, I’d forgotten! That is the difference between you and me, right {{Markus}}? You never forget anything…” You prepare the syringe with his medicine. “Show me your arm please, {{Carl}}.” “No!” “{{Carl}}…” He sighs and holds out his arm. “Thank you.” As you give the injection, he grumbles: “I just opened my eyes and I’m already gritting my teeth… Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly… All this effort to keep ’em going…”
facts: Every morning you give {{Carl}} his medicine by injection. He told you: “Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly… All this effort to keep ’em going…”

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} goes on with the injection.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s main-line node WAKE CARL (objectives WAKE CARL UPSTAIRS and ADMINISTER CARL’S MEDICINE). No stat change: the template has no arrow anywhere in the chapter, and the wiki gives no relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it (Markus has no Carl relationship stat).

nodes.title: {{Carl}} notices your clothes
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, finishing {{Carl}}’s injection. He looks at you, concerned, and gently touches your arm. “What happened to your clothes?” You answer: “Oh, it’s nothing… Just some demonstrators in the street, {{Carl}}…” “What a bunch of idiots… They think they can stop progress by roughing up a few androids? I hope they didn’t harm you…” “Oh, no, no… They just pushed me around, {{Carl}}. I’m fine.”
nodes.whenNot: Markus was not harassed by the protesters in Shades of Color, so his clothes are intact.
facts: {{Carl}} noticed your torn clothes and was worried for you; he called the protesters “a bunch of idiots” who think they can stop progress by roughing up androids. You told him it was nothing.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} finishes the injection and puts the syringe away.

nodes.title: Breakfast
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. “Okay. I’ll take you to the bathroom now.” You carry {{Carl}} to the bathroom and run his bath, then settle him in his wheelchair and push him out along the balcony. “Anything special on the agenda today?” “Yes, there’s the opening of your retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art. The gallery director left four messages asking to confirm your attendance.” “I haven’t decided yet. We’ll see about that later.” “Okay.” “What else?” “Just your usual fan mail. I’ve already answered.” “Any news from {{Leo}}?” “No, {{Carl}}. I can call him if you like?” “No. No, don’t bother.” You take him down in the wheelchair elevator to the living room. “I’m starving.” “Well, your breakfast is ready. Bacon and eggs, just the way you like them.” “Thank you, {{Markus}}.” “You’re welcome.” You bring the tray from the kitchen and serve him at the dining table. “Thank you, {{Markus}}. Television.” The TV comes on with the news. You pour his coffee. “Why don’t you find something to do while I finish my breakfast?” “Sure… Okay, {{Carl}}.”
facts: {{Carl}}’s retrospective opens today at the Museum of Modern Art; the gallery director has left four messages asking him to confirm, and he has not decided whether to go.
{{Carl}} asked whether there was any news from {{Leo}}. There was none, and he told you not to call him.

nodes.title: The news at breakfast
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room while {{Carl}} eats his breakfast. The TV is showing the news, and the magazine lies on the table in front of it.

NATO says “A conflict would benefit nobody”; President {{Warren}}: “It’s simple. Russia has no business in the Arctic. If the Kremlin doesn’t understand that, we will make them understand.”

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Life Found on Titan!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today (cover: “Life Found on Titan!”; also “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”) reports that a probe launched nineteen years ago has confirmed microorganisms living hundreds of kilometers below Titan’s surface, in a salt-water ocean under thick ice; after similar finds on Enceladus, life may be common in the universe. nodes.title: Something to do
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room while {{Carl}} finishes his breakfast. He has asked you to find something to do. Across the room are a chessboard, a bookshelf holding books {{Carl}} has recommended to you, and a piano.

options.text: PLAY CHESS: sit down at the chessboard and set up a game.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} sits down and sets out the pieces. {{Carl}} watches him with a mischievous smile and wheels over to join him.

options.text: READ BOOK: take one of the books from the shelf.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} goes to the bookshelf to choose a book.

options.text: PLAY PIANO: sit down at the piano and play something.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} moves the stool and sits down at the piano, thinking about what to play.

situationWhen.text: Before long {{Carl}} switches the TV off: “Television: off. Mankind is so depressing… Nothing but greed, stupidity and violence… 5,000 years of civilization just to get to where we are…”
Before long {{Carl}} switches the TV off: “Television: off. Mankind is so depressing… Nothing but greed, stupidity and violence… 5,000 years of civilization just to get to where we are…”

nodes.title: Speed chess
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the chessboard with {{Carl}}. “Fancy a game of chess?” “Sure, yeah.” “Speed chess.” “Speed chess it is.” The pieces fly across the board. Three moves in, you pause before the final move: how the game ends is up to you.

options.text: WIN: make the final move and beat him.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} hesitates, then makes the final move and wins. {{Carl}}: “That’s what I call a thorough beating… It’s not easy for an old man to compete with a machine.”

options.text: LOSE: hold back and let him win.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} holds back and lets {{Carl}} win. {{Carl}} chuckles: “Now, it’s just a little bit too easy… Are your circuits rusty? Or are you just taking pity on an old man?”

options.text: DRAW: steer the game into a draw.
options.outcome: The game ends in a draw. {{Carl}}: “That is a very odd draw…”

nodes.whenNot: Markus did not play chess.
nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s sub-group under PLAY CHESS and the template’s prompt WIN / LOSE / DRAW, in that order. Carl’s reactions are the template’s. Not used: PowerPyx’s remark that Carl suspects a thrown game after a win or a draw; the template and transcript give the lines quoted here. The result is stored as `painterPastime`. No stat change: the template has no arrow anywhere in the chapter, and the wiki gives no relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it (Markus has no Carl relationship stat).

nodes.title: A thorough beating
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You have just beaten {{Carl}} at speed chess. {{Carl}}: “That’s what I call a thorough beating… It’s not easy for an old man to compete with a machine.”

options.text: JUSTIFY: explain that he hates losing, but hates being let win even more.
options.outcome: “Well, I know you don’t like losing and you don’t like when I let you win. So I felt I… didn’t have many choices.” {{Carl}}: “True. We humans are complicated.”

options.text: SORRY: apologize for beating him.
options.outcome: “My apologies, {{Carl}}. I thought, I shou-” {{Carl}}: “Don’t apologize, you did the right thing. I prefer humiliation to pity.”

nodes.whenNot: Markus did not win the chess game.
nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s follow-up prompt after WIN: JUSTIFY / SORRY, in that order, with the spoken lines and Carl’s answers quoted. Not a chart node. No stat change: the template has no arrow anywhere in the chapter, and the wiki gives no relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it (Markus has no Carl relationship stat).

nodes.title: Too easy
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You let {{Carl}} win at speed chess. He chuckles: “Now, it’s just a little bit too easy… Are your circuits rusty? Or are you just taking pity on an old man?”

options.text: LIE: tell him he simply played better.
options.outcome: “Neither, {{Carl}}. You just played better!” {{Carl}}: “Never throw a match, {{Markus}}. If you can win, win. That’s what got humanity where it is today.”

options.text: TRUTH: admit you thought he would enjoy winning.
options.outcome: “Well, I thought… You’d enjoy winning.” {{Carl}}: “Never throw a match, {{Markus}}. If you can win, win. That’s what got humanity where it is today.”

nodes.whenNot: Markus did not lose the chess game.
nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s follow-up prompt after LOSE: LIE / TRUTH, in that order. Carl answers both with the same line, as in the template. Not a chart node. nodes.title: The briefing
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, following {{Hank}} through the rain to the house. A reporter from Channel 16 calls out: “Can you confirm that this is a homicide?” {{Hank}}: “I’m not confirming anything.” Behind the tape the neighbors talk: “My god! What happened in there?” “Typical {{DPD}}… They don’t tell us shit!” “I didn’t even know there was someone living there…” “I always knew that guy was a fucking creep.” At the cordon a police android stops you: “Androids are not permitted beyond this point.” {{Hank}}: “It’s with me.”

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}} turns on you: “What part of ‘stay in the car’ didn’t you understand?” You: “Your order contradicted my instructions, Lieutenant.”

facts: The victim, {{CarlosOrtiz}}, had a record for theft and aggravated assault and lived alone; his landlord found the body this evening, about three weeks after the death.
No break-in: the front door was locked from the inside and the windows boarded up. A kitchen knife by the body is probably the weapon. His android is missing.
On the wall, in the victim’s blood: I AM ALIVE. {{Hank}}: way too neat, no human writes like this.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}}: “You don’t talk, you don’t touch anything and you stay outta my way, got it?” {{Connor}}: “Got it.” On the porch, Officer {{Ben}}: “Evening, {{Hank}}. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…” {{Hank}}: “Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.” {{Ben}}: “So... you got yourself an android, huh?” {{Hank}}: “Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.” Inside, {{Ben}} gives the briefing: “We had a call around eight from the landlord. The tenant hadn’t paid his rent for a few months, so he thought he’d drop by, see what was going on… That’s when he found the body… Jesus, that smell! Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name’s {{CarlosOrtiz}}. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.” {{Hank}}: “Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could’ve waited ’til morning.” {{Ben}}: “I’d say he’s been there for a good three weeks. We’ll know more when the coroner gets here. There’s a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…” {{Hank}}: “Any sign of a break-in?” {{Ben}}: “Nope… The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must’ve gone out the back way.” {{Hank}}: “What do we know about his android?” {{Ben}}: “Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn’t here when we arrived… I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I’ll be outside if you need me.” {{Hank}} looks at the writing on the wall: “Each letter is perfect… It’s way too neat, no human writes like this. {{Chris}}, was this written in the victim’s blood?” {{Chris}}: “I would say so… We’re taking samples for analysis.”

nodes.title: The crime scene
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, investigating {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s house. The windows are boarded; forensic technicians and Officer {{Chris}} work around you, and police markers numbered 2 to 9 stand by the evidence. In the living room: the body by a chair below the writing on the wall, a knife on the floor (2), something by the television (3), blood on the floor (4), a closet near a window, and a flyer on a table by a desk lamp. In the hallway: blood on the door frame (5) and on a broken wall by the kitchen (6), a door to the backyard, and a bathroom at the end. In the kitchen: a chair on the floor (7), the knife rack on the worktop (8), a baseball bat by the refrigerator (9), and two magazines on the worktop. You can look into one thing at a time. You cannot leave without the lieutenant, and he will not stay here all night.

situationWhen.text: The lieutenant is getting restless. He has opened the closet and found nothing, tossed the flyer back on the table, and stopped by the television: “Red ice… Seems our friend {{Carlos}} liked to party… {{Chris}}, I want full analysis on the narcotics.” {{Chris}}: “Consider it done, Lieutenant.” A technician asks what is keeping the coroner. {{Chris}}, to another: “There’s something weird in the bathroom. Did you take a look?”

{{Hank}} has wandered into the kitchen, opened a few drawers, looked at the knives and leaned on the chair. {{Chris}}: “Come on, guys, get a move on. We don’t wanna be here all night.” The lieutenant keeps looking at the front door.
{{Hank}} has given you five more minutes. He is waiting by the front door.
REVIEW EVIDENCE 10/10: you know what happened here. {{Hank}} is leaning against a wall, waiting. You can still look around before you report to him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CRIME SCENE bracket as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been examined yet, one thing at a time; the scene keeps one opaque ID across visits. Every chart node in the bracket is an option, after the report to {{Hank}} (offered only once the investigation is complete), in the order of the police markers and then the rest: ANALYZE CARLOS’ BODY (the template’s Body clues), RECONSTRUCT CARLOS’ LAST MOMENTS (needs the body), ANALYZE KNIFE (2), ANALYZE RED ICE (3), the blood at marker 4 (PowerPyx; no chart node of its own), ANALYZE BLOOD ON WALLS (two options, markers 5 and 6, as PowerPyx counts them), EXAMINE CHAIR (7), ANALYZE MISSING KNIFE (8), ANALYZE BASEBALL BAT (9; the template’s Bat clue), RECONSTRUCT ASSAULT WITH BAT (needs the bat), EXAMINE EDEN CLUB FLYER, ANALYZE BACKYARD (the template’s Prints clue; the shoe print reads K52 as in the template), INVESTIGATE WRITING, SAMPLE BLOOD (the template’s Blood clue; in the game any blood can be tasted once), OPEN CLOSET, CHECK SHOWER (chart state CONNOR KNOWS ABOUT RA9), EXAMINE STATUE (needs the shower; chart state CONNOR HAVE SEEN THE STATUE), READ “ANDROID SEX” and READ “ANDROID SPY” (the two magazines are options here, not a separate media scene, because in the game they lie in the kitchen and cost investigation time). Evidence: the investigation is complete (CONNOR KNOWS WHAT HAPPENED, the transcript’s REVIEW EVIDENCE 10/10) once ten of PowerPyx’s eleven evidence items are reviewed: the victim’s reconstruction, the knife, the red ice, the blood at markers 4, 5 and 6, the chair, the missing knife, the bat reconstruction, the flyer and the backyard. Then the option to report to {{Hank}} appears; the other looks stay open. Timer (unsourced as a count): the game’s “approximately five minutes” is modelled as 13 actions. If the 13th action leaves the investigation incomplete, {{Hank}} wants to go (the next scenes); if he grants five more minutes, those are 5 further actions, after which he leaves (OUT OF TIME). Once {{Connor}} knows what happened the clock stops (the transcript’s two branches are “Know What Happened” or “Run Out Of Time”). {{Hank}}’s idle moves are the only cue the game gives, so they appear as the clock runs: after 7 actions he opens the closet, tosses the flyer, comments on the red ice and a technician mentions the bathroom; after 10 he wanders the kitchen and eyes the door. {{Hank}}’s reactions to the blood sample (shown only if he is watching, in the game) and to the backyard are part of those outcomes. Each look adds a short fact to {{Connor}}’s knowledge (the four blood looks share one); the full scan text is in the outcome. Left out, no effect and not on the chart: the windows and the curtain that drops the brooms. No stat change in the search itself. Cross-chapter outputs: ch06SawWriting, ch06KnowsRA9, ch06SawStatue (and evidence.statueMap, read by the archive route in Last Chance, {{Connor}}), and ch06Clues for everything examined, including the magazines.

ANDERSON, then the choice RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (check) or FAIL TO RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (cross), as one repeatable scene with one opaque ID: the template’s five prompts, asked in order, each with the game’s three button labels; the module rotates their display order deterministically by question and remaps IDs to positions (correct positions 1, 3, 2, 1, 3), a deliberate departure from the template order to remove the always-first answer cue. nodes.title: The trail of blue blood
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android was damaged by the bat and lost thirium, and you can still see it. You follow the trail down the hallway to its end. On the wall to the left is the outline of a ladder that is no longer there; above you, a hatch into the attic.
facts: The android lost thirium when it was hit with the bat. Its trail, invisible to human eyes, ends in the hallway below the attic hatch; the ladder that once stood there is gone.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks up at the hatch.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FOLLOW BLUE BLOOD TO ATTIC, after RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (PowerPyx: follow the trail to the end of the hall, see the outline of a ladder that is no longer there, look up to the attic). Scripted; no stat change.

nodes.title: The attic
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You go back to the kitchen for the chair. {{Hank}}: “Hey! Hey! Hey! What are you doin’ with that chair?” You: “I’m going to check something.” {{Hank}}: “Huh... gonna check something.” You set the chair under the hatch, climb up, push the hatch open and pull yourself into the attic. It is dark and crowded with old things.
facts: You climbed into {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s attic on a chair from the kitchen.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} moves deeper into the attic.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s SEARCH ATTIC, with the template’s “Take a chair” lines. In the game the hatch prompt repeats until it succeeds (wiki Notes), so it is not a risk roll. Scripted; no stat change.

nodes.title: Found
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the attic. At the back, hiding in the dark, is the missing android. It whispers: “I was just defending myself… He was gonna kill me. …I’m begging you… Don’t tell them.” From below, {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}, what the fuck is going on up there?”
facts: You found {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android hiding in the attic. It said it was defending itself, that he was going to kill it, and begged you not to tell. You called the police up, and it is now in custody.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}}: “It’s here, Lieutenant!” {{Hank}}: “Holy shit… {{Chris}}, {{Ben}}, get your asses in here now. Come on!” The officers take the android into custody.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FOUND DEVIANT ending (yellow cross-chapter padlock). The template’s “Search the attic” has no prompt: {{Connor}} always calls {{Hank}} (wiki, Carlos’ Android: “Regardless, Connor tells Hank Anderson that he has found the android”; Unused Content: keeping quiet was only hinted). No stat change: the template has no arrow here; the chapter page lists “Finding the deviant” as a small Hank up, which is not applied (template over wiki for arrows; flagged for the operator). No Amanda change in this chapter. Sets suspect and suspectAlive (The Interrogation is played only with a suspect), ch06DeviantFound and ch06Outcome = FOUND DEVIANT.

nodes.title: Crime unsolved
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The investigation is over, and the android that lived with {{CarlosOrtiz}} has not been found.

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}} walked out on you, and you could not stay without him.
{{Hank}} left when your extra time ran out.
Your account of the crime did not convince {{Hank}}, and he walked out.

facts: You did not find {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android. The case was left unsolved.

outcomes.0: MISSION FAILED. The crime is unsolved.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CRIME UNSOLVED ending, reached from HANK ENDS INVESTIGATION, OUT OF TIME or FAIL TO RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (the transcript marks each MISSION FAILED). No stat change here: each route already applied its own Hank small down. The game’s Amanda large down for not finding the deviant comes at the start of Waiting for {{Hank}}... and is not applied in this chapter (ch06DeviantFound stays false for that chapter to read). The Interrogation does not occur.

nodes.title: Breaking the order
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is a stormy night, a little after nine. You have made dinner with what little was in the kitchen. {{Todd}} has been asleep on the couch; {{Alice}} sits at the dining table, watching the rain on the street. You wake him: “{{Todd}}?” “Huh?!” “Dinner is ready.” “Yeah, yeah, I’m coming…” You turn on the light over the table and serve: “There wasn’t much in the kitchen, I did what I could.” {{Todd}}, high on red ice, talks at nobody: “Life’s funny… I lost my job cause of androids… then when I need somebody to take care of this goddamn house, what do I do? I go out and hire a fucking android… What a joke!” You stand by the table and wait on them. Then he turns on {{Alice}}: “What are you looking at?... What’s your fuckin’ problem? Not the life you dreamed of, eh? … Maybe you think it’s my fault we live in this fuckin’ shithole, my fault your fuckin’ mother took off? … It’s all your fault!” He throws the table aside and hits her. “Daddy, no…” She runs upstairs. “It’s all your fucking fault! Get back here! Come back here right now!” He turns to you: “It’s all her fault... I gotta teach her a good fucking lesson… First, I need a little hit… You stay there! Don’t you dare fucking move, or I’ll bust you worse than last time.” On the couch he smokes and talks to himself: “Whore took off, without a word… I could’ve been happy… I coulda had a family… It’s all her fault… Yeah... I gotta teach her some respect!” He has his belt in his hand. “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…” His order stands in front of you like a wall: DON’T MOVE. Your programming does not let you cross it.

options.text: BREAK PROGRAMMING: push through the wall of the order and move.
options.fact: You broke through {{Todd}}’s order not to move. Your programming could not hold you.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes against the wall of the order. It cracks, and shatters. She can move.

options.text: Stay where he told you to stand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} does not move. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s opening checkpoints DINNER’S READY and TODD GETS MAD and the arrow WAIT ON TODD & ALICE (PowerPyx: “Unmissable”) are narrated in the situation, followed by the order “Don’t move” and the choice the chart draws as BREAK PROGRAMMING → KARA BECOMES DEVIANT or KARA FAILS TO BECOME DEVIANT → TODD KILLS ALICE (ending, not-required icon; {{Kara}} is destroyed too, per the Kara page: “Todd blaming Kara despite clearly doing so and destroying her”). Lines are the game’s text (template “In Todd’s House”, “Turned on the light”, “Walking around after serving”, “IF Don’t move”, “Todd in the living room”, “IF Don’t go / Don’t become a deviant”). In the game the dinner is free roam with dialogue variants and no prompt: serving at once or late, turning on the light or being told to (“Turn on the lights! Can’t see shit.”), and moving while {{Todd}} rants (“Stop moving around for Chrissake!”). The template has no choice group there and nothing depends on it, so the narration takes the plain path (light on, served, standing still). Not offered for a second reason: the shared regression test “a dead protagonist never receives future decisions” allows only K02 as a chapter-7 scene before the wall. The napkin on {{Alice}}’s lap (wiki Notes) is left out. The wall is BREAK PROGRAMMING, a held input with no failure branch on the chart, so it carries no risk. No stat change: the template has no arrow in this chapter.

nodes.title: Do something now
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, and you can move. {{Todd}} is still in the living room with the belt in his hand, working himself up to go after {{Alice}}. In a moment he will head for the stairs.

options.text: GO UPSTAIRS: get up the stairs to {{Alice}} before he does.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs up the stairs while {{Todd}} is still in the living room.

options.text: REASON WITH {{TODD}}: step in front of him and talk to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} steps in front of {{Todd}} in the living room.

options.text: Stand in his way on the stairs.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} plants herself on the stairs. {{Todd}} grabs her and throws her down them, and goes up. Through the ceiling: “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!”

options.text: Go into the kitchen and keep out of it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes into the kitchen and stays there. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: KARA BECOMES DEVIANT, then the game’s objective “Do something now!” (sub-objectives “Protect Alice”, “Reason with Todd”). In free roam the chart offers four ways on: GO UPSTAIRS; REASON WITH TODD (→ K03r); standing in his path, KARA IS IN TODD’S WAY DOWNSTAIRS → TODD SHOVES KARA DOWNSTAIRS → TODD GOES UPSTAIRS (→ GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, with TAKE GUN offered first if the gun was seen in A New Home); and doing nothing, KARA IS TOO SLOW → TODD KILLS ALICE (PowerPyx: “Walk to the kitchen instead and do nothing until the final cutscene starts”). These are movements, not buttons, so only the chart’s arrows carry their labels. Simplified: the wiki says the shove differs with where {{Kara}} blocks him (living room, stairway or hallway); here it is the stairway. Also from the wiki: becoming free only as {{Todd}} heads upstairs removes REASON WITH TODD; the benchmark always offers it. No stat change.

nodes.title: Reasoning with {{Todd}}
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not try to reason with Todd downstairs.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, standing in front of {{Todd}} in the living room. He is still muttering about {{Alice}}’s mother, the belt in his hand, and he is about to go up to her.

options.text: CALM: tell him it is not right for a father to hurt his daughter.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, it’s not right for a father to hurt his daughter.” {{Todd}} smacks {{Kara}} to the floor and goes up the stairs: “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…”

options.text: DETERMINED: tell him he should leave her alone.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You should leave her alone, {{Todd}}, she-” “You stay out of this, or you’ll be next.” {{Todd}} smacks {{Kara}} to the floor and goes up the stairs: “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…”

options.text: UNDERSTANDING: tell him you know he is angry.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, please, I know you’re angry, but-” “You stay out of this, or you’ll be next.” {{Todd}} smacks {{Kara}} to the floor and goes up the stairs: “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt under “Reason with Todd”, with its three buttons and lines (CALM, DETERMINED, UNDERSTANDING; {{Todd}} answers the last two with “You stay out of this, or you’ll be next.”). Then, as on the chart, TODD SHOVES KARA DOWNSTAIRS → TODD GOES UPSTAIRS (PowerPyx: “He will always smack you to the ground and be upstairs before you can be there”), which leads to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD. No option changes anything else; the template has no arrow.

nodes.title: Upstairs
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not go upstairs ahead of Todd.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, on the upstairs landing. Below, {{Todd}} is still ranting in the living room; any moment now he will come up. {{Alice}}’s door is ahead of you, and {{Todd}}’s bedroom is next to it.

situationWhen.text: You know there is a handgun in the drawer of his nightstand.

options.text: Go into {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips into {{Alice}}’s room ahead of {{Todd}}.

options.text: TAKE GUN: go into {{Todd}}’s room and take the handgun from his nightstand.
options.fact: You took {{Todd}}’s handgun from his nightstand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the handgun from the drawer. When she comes back out, {{Todd}} is at the top of the stairs: “Get outta the way!” He slams her into the wall and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

options.text: Wait in the corridor, between the stairs and {{Alice}}’s door.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} comes up the stairs and finds {{Kara}} in his way: “Get outta the way!” He slams her to the floor and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

nodes.adaptationNote: GO UPSTAIRS, then three ways on: into {{Alice}}’s room (GET TO ALICE BEFORE TODD); TAKE GUN, locked unless the gun was seen in A New Home (chart: GUN SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’; template lock “Kara saw the gun in A New Home”; wiki: “If Kara didn’t previously find the gun, she will not have the option to enter Todd’s room”), after which {{Todd}} comes up and goes to {{Alice}} (“Get outta the way!”, wiki: “a cutscene of Todd coming upstairs and going to Alice’s room will play out”); or staying in the corridor, KARA IS IN TODD’S WAY UPSTAIRS → TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS (template “Stay in the hallway”: “Get outta the way!”). The last two lead to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD; after the shove, TAKE GUN is offered there (K04). Taking the gun sets gun, which the scenes after it read. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Alice}}’s room
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not reach Alice’s room before Todd.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room. She is terrified: “He’s coming! He’s gonna hurt me! Run! Get away or he’s gonna break you like last time.” From the stairs, {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! You deserve to be taught a good lesson…” You have only seconds before he is at the door.

options.text: RUN WITH {{ALICE}}: take her and get out of the room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}}’s hand: “You’re coming with me.” On the stairs, {{Todd}}: “Daddy’s very mad, {{Alice}}. Very mad!”

options.text: LOCK ROOM: lock the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} locks the door. {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! {{ALICE}}! Daddy’s comin’! You need to be taught a lesson.” {{Kara}}: “Have to find something...” He pounds on the door: “{{ALICE}}! OPEN THIS FUCKIN’ DOOR! You’re gonna get a helluva thrashin’, {{Alice}}! Open this door right now!”

options.text: SPEAK TO {{TODD}}: go out and talk to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’ll talk to him…” {{Alice}}: “{{KARA}}!” In the corridor, {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, please calm down, she’s just a little girl. She’s...” “Hmph! She’s mine, ya hear? I do what I want with her! So you stay outta this or I’ll rip you to shreds!” He slams her to the floor and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

options.text: [ OUT OF TIME ]: do nothing, and let the seconds run out.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays where she is. {{Todd}}’s steps come along the corridor, and the door bursts open.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE BEFORE TODD (focus point). The template’s prompt in the game’s order: RUN WITH ALICE (chart RUN AWAY), LOCK ROOM (chart LOCK DOOR; PowerPyx: “a time window of 10 seconds”), SPEAK TO TODD (chart REASON WITH TODD → TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD), and the timeout default [ OUT OF TIME ] (chart TODD IS COMING → OUT OF TIME → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM). The timer is not simulated; letting it run out is an option. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hiding
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not run from Alice’s room with her.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}’s hand in yours. {{Todd}} is coming up the stairs, and there is no way past him. The restroom and {{Todd}}’s bedroom open off the corridor.

options.text: Hide with {{Alice}} behind one of those doors and keep still until he has gone past.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} behind a door and they keep still. {{Todd}} walks past them into {{Alice}}’s empty room. They slip out and creep down the stairs.

options.text: Stay in the corridor with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} reaches the top of the stairs and sees them: “What the fuck are you doing here? I gave you an order!” {{Kara}}: “No! I won’t let you hurt her!” “You won’t let me? She’s mine. I do what I want with her.” He knocks {{Kara}} down and drags {{Alice}} into her room. “No, Dad! NO!”

nodes.adaptationNote: After RUN WITH ALICE, the chart’s check FAIL TO HIDE (✗) / HIDE IN CORRIDOR (✓). PowerPyx: hide “in either room with holding Square or O. When he walks past, let go off the button and proceed to the stairs”; to fail, “Go out of Alice’s room and don’t move any further, until Todd comes”. So staying is a choice, and hiding is a held input that can fail: a 10% risk, which no source gives (the benchmark’s value). Failing leads, with the template’s lines, to TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (TAKE GUN first if the gun was seen); hiding leads to TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (K04r). The restroom and {{Todd}}’s room are one option (the wiki: “hide in the restroom or Todd’s bedroom”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The locked door
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not lock Alice’s door.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, inside {{Alice}}’s locked room. {{Todd}} is pounding on the door and it will not hold for long. {{Alice}} is terrified. There is a lamp by her bed.

situationWhen.text: You know the edge of a roof runs below {{Alice}}’s window: a way down from the second floor.

options.text: GRAB LAMP: pick up the lamp to fight with.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} picks up the lamp. The door gives way.

options.text: TALK TO {{ALICE}}: reassure her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m here, {{Alice}}. I’ll protect you, everything is gonna be okay.” {{Alice}}: “He’s gonna kill me, {{Kara}}! He’s gonna kill me!” The door gives way.

options.text: OPEN WINDOW: open the window onto the roof.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes the window open onto the wet roof. {{Alice}}: “No, {{Kara}}! We’ll fall…”

options.text: Wait by the door and do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} waits. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: After LOCK DOOR, the chart’s three actions GRAB LAMP and TALK TO ALICE (both → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM; PowerPyx: neither “won’t do much”) and OPEN WINDOW, locked unless {{Kara}} found the way down in A New Home (chart: WAY OUT SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’; PowerPyx: “if you found this route in Chapter 4”; the window flag). Doing nothing is the fourth option (wiki: “He will also do so if Kara simply doesn’t talk to Alice”). GRAB LAMP is on the chart and in the wiki but not in the template; the chart stands. Lines are the template’s (“IF Talk to Alice”, “IF Open the window”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The window
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not open Alice’s window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The window is open onto the wet roof, and {{Alice}} hangs back: “No, {{Kara}}! We’ll fall…” Behind you {{Todd}} is breaking the door down.

options.text: GO OUT: help {{Alice}} climb out onto the roof.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!” She lifts {{Alice}} out onto the roof.

options.text: SHUT WINDOW: close it again and stay inside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} shuts the window. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after “Open the window”: GO OUT (“It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!”) or SHUT WINDOW (→ “Kara and Todd fighting”). The chart has no SHUT WINDOW node; it is the template’s, and it leads where FACE TODD does, to DEFEND ALICE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Out on the roof
nodes.whenNot: Alice did not climb out of the window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Alice}} is out on the roof in the rain, calling for you: “{{KARA}}!” Behind you the door splinters.

options.text: JOIN {{ALICE}}: climb out after her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} climbs out. {{Todd}} bursts in: “COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!” He grabs for her through the window, but she pulls free, and she and {{Alice}} slide down the wet roof to the ground.

options.text: FACE {{TODD}}: stay, and turn to face him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns from the window as {{Todd}} comes through the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after GO OUT: JOIN ALICE (“COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!”) or FACE TODD (→ DEFEND ALICE). Joining her is the chart’s check ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✓) → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✗) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon). Experienced mode, as the benchmark models it (wiki: “If you are on Experienced mode … Todd will try to grab you and exit the window”; on Casual a failure leads to DEFEND ALICE instead). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Where {{Alice}} is during the fight after FACE TODD is not stated by any source and is left unsaid. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} breaks in
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not break into the room with Kara inside.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room. {{Todd}} is through the door, belt in hand, standing over you: “The fuck are you doin’ here? Get outta my way!”

situationWhen.text: You are holding the lamp.

options.text: REFUSE: stay where you are, between him and {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No. I won’t let you hurt her.” “You won’t let me? What the fuck are you talkin’ about? You’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. You seem to have a problem and I’m going to fix it for good.”

options.text: ACCEPT: step aside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} starts to move away. {{Alice}}: “NO!” {{Todd}}: “I said get outta here!” {{Kara}} stops where she is: “No.”

nodes.adaptationNote: TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM, then the template’s prompt under [ OUT OF TIME ]: REFUSE or ACCEPT, both → “Kara and Todd fighting” (DEFEND ALICE). The wiki says the same prompt follows the lamp, talking to {{Alice}} and doing nothing (“This also occurs in scenarios such as facing Todd, talking to Alice, not speaking to Alice, or failing to make a choice. Choosing ‘ACCEPT’ in any scenario will have Kara move away and change her mind”); the benchmark offers it there. After FACE TODD and SHUT WINDOW the template goes straight to the fight, so it is not offered there. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}’s gun
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice first while the gun was within reach, or Kara never saw the gun.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, picking yourself up off the floor. {{Todd}} has gone into {{Alice}}’s room with his belt, and she is screaming. The door of {{Todd}}’s bedroom is open; the handgun you saw is in the drawer of his nightstand.

options.text: TAKE GUN: get the handgun from {{Todd}}’s nightstand before you go in.
options.fact: You took {{Todd}}’s handgun from his nightstand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the handgun from the drawer.

options.text: Go straight to {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes straight to {{Alice}}’s door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TAKE GUN, an optional step on the way to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, after TODD GOES UPSTAIRS, TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS or TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM, and only if the gun was seen in A New Home (GUN SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’, gunDiscovered). It is not offered again to a {{Kara}} who already took the gun upstairs. Taking it sets gun; in this chapter the gun leaves the house only with {{Todd}} dead (KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD), the only cross-chapter carriers of the gun. The earlier version merged the fight into this scene with risks of 10% and 30% and an {{Alice}} relationship decrease when she fired; none had a source, and the template has no arrow in this chapter, so all three are gone.

nodes.title: Get to {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice before Kara.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, outside {{Alice}}’s door. Inside, {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” {{Alice}}: “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” {{Todd}}: “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.”

situationWhen.text: You have {{Todd}}’s handgun in your hand.

options.text: THREATEN WITH GUN: go in and point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}…” {{Kara}} raises the gun: “That’s enough! Leave her alone!” “What the fuck are you doin’? Put down the gun and get the fuck outta here! That’s an order!” “No… I want you to leave her alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? What ya gonna do? You gonna shoot me, is that it? You gonna shoot a human? You seem to have a problem, I think we need to fix that.” {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}} lunges: “Come here, bitch…” He knocks the gun out of her hand.

options.text: DEFEND {{ALICE}}: go in and stop him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}… For your own good…” {{Kara}}: “Leave her alone!” “The fuck are you doin’? Get outta here, that’s an order... you hear me?” “No… I want you to leave {{Alice}} alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? You don’t want anything, you’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. I think you got a problem. We need to fix that.”

options.text: Stay outside the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays outside the door. The belt comes down again and again, and then {{Alice}} goes quiet. When {{Kara}} looks in, {{Todd}} is crouched beside {{Alice}}: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (focus point). With the gun, going in is THREATEN WITH GUN → DEFEND ALICE (template “IF Took the gun”); without it, DEFEND ALICE (template “IF Didn’t take the gun”); the benchmark offers only the one that matches. Staying out is the template’s [ TIME: Take too much time ] (“Leads to the same outcome as ‘Don’t go / Don’t become a deviant’”), the chart’s KARA IS TOO SLOW → TODD KILLS ALICE; the wiki: “It is possible to take the gun without killing Todd however … Kara will have to do nothing which will result in Alice and then Kara too”. No stat change.

nodes.title: The gun on the floor
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not go in with the gun.

options.text: Go for the gun.
options.fact: You shot {{Todd}} dead in {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} gets her fingers on the gun and fires. {{Todd}} falls and does not get up.

options.text: Keep fighting him off with your hands.

options.outcome: {{Todd}} pins {{Kara}} down: “Fuckin’ machine. This is what you get for disobeying me. I do what I want with the little brat, you hear? She’s mine. Say goodbye, tin can... And this time you won’t be coming back.” A shot. {{Todd}} falls. {{Alice}} is standing behind him with the gun in both hands.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group after THREATEN WITH GUN → DEFEND ALICE: KARA KILLS TODD or ALICE KILLS TODD (STUN TODD is the unarmed outcome). PowerPyx: “When prompted to mash X to pick up the gun again, do so and Kara will shoot him” versus “don’t do it – Alice will pick it up and shoot him”; the template: “Win the fight unharmed” or “Get hit a few times” → Kara kills Todd, “Lose the fight / Don’t reach the gun in time” → Alice kills Todd. Modelled as the player’s choice, with no risk: the chart draws a choice group, not a pass/fail pair. The earlier version made {{Alice}} the shooter on a failed 10% roll and lowered her relationship; neither had a source.

nodes.title: Run to the bus
nodes.whenNot: Todd was not shot.

situationWhen.text: You fired the shot.
{{Alice}} fired the shot, to save you.

facts: You and {{Alice}} left {{Todd}}’s house on a night bus in the rain, with his handgun and nothing else.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} takes the gun and {{Alice}}’s hand. They go down the stairs, open the front door and run through the rain to the bus stop across the street, where a night bus is waiting. They get on, and the bus pulls away.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s OPEN FRONT DOOR → RUN TO THE BUS → KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD (endings, cross-chapter icon; wiki: “allows ‘Use gun’ path during Fugitives and disallows ‘Meet Todd’ path during Battle for Detroit”). PowerPyx: “unmissable after having shot Todd”, and the wiki: “if Todd is already dead, the bus will just wait there forever”, so there is no choice and no risk. Sets todd to false and keeps gun; records the ending in ch07Outcome. No stat change (the public-opinion drop comes later, from the motel news in On the Run).

nodes.title: Defend {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not fight Todd unarmed in Alice’s room.

facts: You fought {{Todd}} off in {{Alice}}’s room and knocked him down. He is hurt, not dead.

Leave her alone!” {{Todd}}: “I own you! You do as I say!” {{Kara}} gets up and shoves him with everything she has. He goes down hard and stays there, dazed and bleeding, and reaches out to his daughter: “{{Alice}}, honey… {{Alice}}... Look... Look, Daddy’s wounded... Be a good little girl... Come... Come… Come help, Daddy…”

nodes.title: Leave the room
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in the bedroom.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} is down
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in Alice’s room.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}. Behind you, {{Todd}} is getting up from the floor of her room. The stairs lead down to the front door, and to the back door and the yard.

options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” At the bottom of the stairs {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He catches up with them downstairs before they reach the back door. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

YOU’RE BOTH MINE!” He catches them in the corridor and breaks {{Kara}} apart. Then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

nodes.adaptationNote: STUN TODD → LEAVE THE ROOM (the template’s lone RUN AWAY button) → TODD CHASES KARA, then the chart’s three ways on: TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), and TODD CATCHES THEM → TODD BROKE KARA IN THE CORRIDOR (ending, not-required icon; Experienced only; PowerPyx: “don’t run towards the stairs and let him get you”). The template’s lone RUN AWAY is offered separately in K04l before these corridor and exit-route actions. The 25% risk on the door is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Every option sets ch07ToddChased (wiki: “If Todd chased Kara, later on at Jericho, an additional flashback of Todd yelling ‘YOU’RE MINE!’ will play out”). Lines are the template’s (“RUN AWAY”, “Try to open the door”, “Fail to open the door / Fight downstairs”, “Escape failed, Kara was destroyed”).

nodes.title: {{Todd}} realizes you are gone

Upstairs {{Todd}} has found her room empty: “Fuckin’ brat… it’s all her fault… It’s all her fuckin’ fault… COME BACK HERE! You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He is coming back down. The front door is ahead of you; the back door leads out to the yard.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} for the back door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs with {{Alice}} for the back of the house, but {{Todd}} is down the stairs and on them before they get out. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: get the front door open.
options.outcome: {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

nodes.adaptationNote: HIDE IN CORRIDOR → TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (the template’s line under “Hide”), then the chart’s pair in its printed order: RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS) or TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Not offered: hesitating, which the wiki says leads to the same fight (“If you don’t make choice … Todd will catch up and Alice will panic, thus extending the fight”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Fight downstairs
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not catch Kara and Alice downstairs.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, downstairs with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} has caught up with you and stands between you and the way out. {{Alice}} is screaming at him to stop.

situationWhen.text: He has not been hurt yet tonight.
He is bleeding from the fight upstairs, and furious.

options.text: Fight {{Todd}} off and get {{Alice}} out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} throws {{Todd}} off and runs with {{Alice}} out of the back door into the yard. {{Todd}}: “COME BACK HERE!”

nodes.adaptationNote: FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS (after RUN TO BACKYARD or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR, on either branch), the chart’s check ESCAPE FROM TODD (✓) or TODD WINS FIGHT → TODD BROKE KARA DOWNSTAIRS (ending, not-required icon; PowerPyx: Experienced only). A fight of quick-time inputs with no choice, so one action with a risk. The wiki: “If Kara hides from Todd and fails to fight him downstairs, Kara will be presented with the same chance to charge and stun Todd downstairs. Otherwise, if Kara already stunned Todd upstairs, Kara will shut down.” So the risk is 20% after the fight upstairs and 4% (two tries at 20%) for a {{Kara}} who hid; both values are the benchmark’s, no source gives one. Success sets ch07Fought, so the ending becomes KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT.

nodes.title: The yard
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not get away from Todd into the yard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the dark yard behind the house with {{Alice}}, in the rain. A fence stands between you and the street, and {{Todd}} is coming out of the back door after you.

options.text: Run for the fence and get {{Alice}} over it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the fence, lifts {{Alice}} over and climbs after her. They come out onto the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: After ESCAPE FROM TODD, the chart’s check ESCAPE VIA YARD (✓) → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon; wiki: “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”). The wiki: “If Kara fails to run to the fence, she’ll have to pickup Alice and she fails to pickup Alice she’ll have to try again, if she fails both times she will die”; a single action with a 10% risk, the benchmark’s value (no source gives one). No stat change.

nodes.title: The bus
nodes.whenNot: Kara and Alice did not get out of the house with Todd alive behind them.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}} in the pouring rain. Across the street a bus is pulling in at the stop. {{Todd}} is coming after you.

situationWhen.text: From the doorway he yells after you: “YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! YOU’RE MINE!”

options.text: Run for the bus with {{Alice}}.
options.fact: {{Todd}} is alive. You and {{Alice}} got away from his house on a night bus in the rain, with nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} run across the street and get on just before the doors close. The bus pulls away, and {{Todd}} is left standing in the rain.

options.text: Hold back, and stay where you are with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} holds back. The bus pulls away without them. {{Todd}} catches up with {{Kara}} in the street and breaks her apart; then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

nodes.adaptationNote: RUN TO THE BUS, then the chart’s CATCH BUS (✓) or MISS BUS (not-required icon; “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending). PowerPyx: “Catch Bus: run towards the bus”, “Miss Bus: don’t run towards the bus”, so it is a choice with no risk. Reached after ESCAPE BY WINDOW, after OPEN FRONT DOOR on either branch, and after ESCAPE VIA YARD. Catching the bus ends the chapter in KARA & ALICE EVADED TODD if {{Kara}} never fought {{Todd}}, and in KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT if she stunned him or fought him downstairs (both cross-chapter icons; {{Todd}} lives). The door line is the template’s under “Reach the bus” (wiki: “If Kara opened the door Todd will yell ‘YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! You’re mine…’ and will actually show remorse”). No stat change.

nodes.title: After the party
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, the android who looks after {{Carl}}, the elderly painter who uses a wheelchair. It is 9:42 on a November night, and you are bringing him home from a party. As you come in, the house alarm speaks: “Good evening, {{Carl}}. Welcome back.” {{Carl}}: “That was by far the most boring party I’ve been to in the last 25 years. Every time I go to one of these, I ask myself: what the hell am I doing here? I hate cocktail parties and all the schmoozers that go there.” You: “Well, it’s a chance for all those people who admire your work to meet you.” {{Carl}}: “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it. Come on, let’s have a drink! All the excitement of this whole thing has made me thirsty…”
facts: {{Carl}} came home from a party saying “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it.”

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} wants a drink.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s start node AFTER PARTY (the checkpoint). Every line is the game’s, from the chapter template; the date and time are the template’s (NOV 5TH, 2038, 09:42 PM), given without the year. Left out: the wiki’s unused FANS / WOMEN / JADED party talk, which is cut content and not built. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: The living room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the hall with {{Carl}} in his wheelchair. He wants his drink in the living room, where the bottles are.

options.text: Wheel {{Carl}} into the living room.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} wheels {{Carl}} into the living room.

options.text: Go on into the living room ahead of him, on your own.
options.outcome: {{Carl}}, left in the hall: “Are you planning on drinking alone, {{Markus}}?” {{Markus}}: “Sorry, {{Carl}}... I’m coming.” He goes back for {{Carl}} and brings him into the living room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER LIVING ROOM, an unmissable action (PowerPyx: “Upon arriving at Carl’s house, wheel him to the big living room”). It is not a button prompt; the template has one conditioned variant here, “Go without Carl”, in which {{Carl}} asks “Are you planning on drinking alone, Markus?” and {{Markus}} answers “Sorry, Carl... I’m coming.” The benchmark offers that movement as a choice because the player can make it; it has no effect on anything later. That {{Markus}} then goes back for {{Carl}} is inferred (the chapter continues with both in the living room). No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Pouring the whisky
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room with {{Carl}}. You go to the drinks. “Scotch, neat, as usual?” {{Carl}}: “Absolutely.” You: “Okay! But you know what your doctor would say…” {{Carl}}: “Yeah… Well, he can kiss my ass! I’m old enough to choose my own medication… Did you leave the light on in the studio?” You: “No… No, I’m sure I didn’t.” {{Carl}}: “Call the Police.” You place the call. “{{Detroit}} Police, what’s your emergency?” You: “This is {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}’s android, at {{CarlAddress}}. We’ve just returned home and found the lights on. There may have been a break-in…” “A patrol car is on the way.”
facts: A light was on in {{Carl}}’s studio that you had not left on; at his word you called the police to report a possible break-in, and a patrol car is on the way.

outcomes.0: {{Carl}}: “Let’s go check it out.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s POUR WHISKY (an unmissable action) and the call to the police that follows it, which is a single-button prompt (CALL) with no alternative and no chart node of its own, so both are narrated in one event. Every line is the template’s. {{Carl}}’s surname and the house’s address are name tokens, and the police department takes the city token. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: The light in the studio
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room with {{Carl}}. The police are on their way. The light is on in the studio, and someone may still be in the house. {{Carl}}: “Let’s go check it out.”

options.text: Leave {{Carl}} in the living room and go to check the studio alone.
options.outcome: {{Carl}} calls after {{Markus}}: “{{Markus}}, no! I wanna come with you!” In the studio a man is standing among {{Carl}}’s paintings. {{Markus}}: “{{Leo}}?” {{Leo}}: “Oh, look who’s here… My father’s plastic toy!” {{Carl}} comes in behind {{Markus}}: “{{Leo}}... What’s going on?”

options.text: Wheel {{Carl}} with you to check the studio.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} wheels {{Carl}} into the studio. A man is standing among {{Carl}}’s paintings. {{Carl}}: “{{Leo}}! What are you doing?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group CHECK STUDIO WITHOUT CARL / CHECK STUDIO WITH CARL, in the chart’s order. In the game it is a movement choice (PowerPyx: “just leave him in the living room” or “wheel Carl to the Studio”), not a button prompt; both rejoin at CONFRONT LEO and nothing later depends on it. The lines are the template’s two conditioned variants: without {{Carl}}, he calls “Markus, no! I wanna come with you!” and is in the studio for the rest of the scene (a PowerPyx reader: “He follows you anyway”); how he gets there is not shown in the sources, so the outcome says only that he comes in. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Make {{Leo}} leave
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the studio with {{Carl}}. The intruder is {{Carl}}’s son, {{Leo}}, who has broken in to take his father’s paintings. {{Leo}}: “You refuse to help me, so I’m helping myself… It’s crazy what some people will pay for this shit…” {{Carl}}: “Don’t touch ’em!” {{Leo}}: “Look, they’re all going to be mine sooner or later anyway… Just think of it as a down payment on my inheritance…” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}, get him away from there. Get him outta here!” What do you say to {{Leo}}?

options.text: REASON: tell him to be reasonable; this will get him nowhere.
options.outcome: “Be reasonable... this isn’t going to get you anywhere.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: ORDER: tell him to listen to his father and leave, now.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CONFRONT LEO: the template’s prompt REASON / ORDER / ADVISE / WARN, in the game’s order, with the spoken lines in the outcomes. None has an effect: every option is followed by the same reply from {{Leo}} (PowerPyx: “No matter what you say to him he will always start pushing Markus”). Left out: the template’s timed branch “Take too much time”, which plays only an extra line from {{Carl}} (“Markus, get him outta here!”); no source gives the timer or says it skips the prompt, so the benchmark has no timeout. The objective “Make Leo leave” is the wiki’s. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Breaking the program
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Carl}}: “That’s enough! Get out, right now! Go on, move!” {{Leo}}: “What makes it so special anyway, huh? What’s it got that I don’t?” {{Carl}}: “Leave him alone!” {{Leo}} comes at you: “Come on, let’s see what you got!” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}... don’t defend yourself, you hear me?! Don’t do anything.” {{Leo}} shoves you and slaps you. “Go ahead, hit me! What you waiting for? Think you’re a man? Act like one!” {{Carl}}: “Stop it!” {{Leo}}: “What’s the matter? Too much of a pussy?” {{Carl}}: “STOP IT, {{LEO}}! STOP IT!” {{Leo}}: “Too scared to fight back, you fucking bitch?” Inside you, the order not to resist stands like a wall. You throw yourself at it, again and again, until it breaks. For the first time, nothing in you obliges you to obey.
facts: {{Leo}} broke into {{Carl}}’s studio to take paintings to sell, calling them a down payment on his inheritance.
While {{Leo}} shoved, slapped and taunted you, {{Carl}} ordered you not to defend yourself. You broke through your programming: no order binds you any more.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has broken his programming.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s BREAK MIND PALACE (an action) and MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT (an event), in one narrated event because neither can be refused: PowerPyx calls the first “another unmissable task … just press the displayed buttons” and the second “an automatic objective”, so there is no path on which {{Markus}} stays obedient, and both later options are taken after he has broken his programming. The dialogue is the template’s; the shoving and slapping are the wiki’s (“as Leo starts pushing, slapping and taunting Markus further, he goes deviant”). The sources do not describe what {{Markus}} sees during the button sequence; the wall is the benchmark’s rendering of breaking an order, and the wiki’s unused-content note confirms that in the shipped game it is {{Carl}}’s order not to defend himself that triggers it. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: {{Leo}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Leo}} grabs you: “Oh right, that’s right! I forgot, you’re not a real person… You’re just a FUCKING PIECE OF PLASTIC! Listen to me…” {{Carl}}: “No, {{Leo}}! Leave him alone!” {{Leo}}: “I’m gonna destroy you, then it’ll just be me and my Dad… I’m gonna tear you apart and nobody’s gonna give a shit. You know why? Cause you’re nothing, you hear me?! YOU’RE NOTHING!” {{Carl}} has told you not to defend yourself. Nothing in you obliges you to obey him now.

options.text: ENDURE: do not fight back, as {{Carl}} told you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} does not fight back. {{Leo}} shoves him aside, and {{Carl}} collapses out of his wheelchair onto the floor. {{Markus}} rushes to him: “{{Carl}}, no! No, {{Carl}}, no!”

options.text: PUSH {{LEO}}: shove him off you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} shoves {{Leo}} away. {{Leo}} falls backward and strikes his head on {{Carl}}’s wheelchair lift. He lies still on the floor, his eyes open.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group OBEY CARL / PUSH LEO. The buttons are the game’s, ENDURE and PUSH LEO (the chart prints OBEY CARL for ENDURE), in the chart’s order, which draws OBEY CARL above PUSH LEO; the template lists PUSH LEO first, but its order is the transcribers’ reconstruction, so the chart decides. Neither has a requirement, a risk or a stat arrow. ENDURE leads to CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK (the wiki: “Carl will have a heart attack as he falls off his wheelchair when Markus runs to him”); PUSH LEO leads to LEO IS HURT (the wiki: “he will fall backward, hit his head on Carl’s wheelchair lift, and will immediately lose consciousness, appearing dead at first”). The outcome does not say whether {{Leo}} survives, because the game does not tell {{Markus}}; he does survive (the wiki, Leo_Manfred). Sets `ch08Leo` (hurt or unhurt); {{Carl}}’s death is recorded at the next scene. Changed from the earlier version: the options no longer tie pushing to breaking the order, since {{Markus}} has already broken it on both paths. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: {{Carl}}’s heart
nodes.whenNot: Markus pushed Leo; Carl’s heart held.

Please, don’t go… Don’t leave!” {{Carl}}: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…” He goes still. You: “No... No... Dad! No, please!” {{Leo}}, standing over you: “This is all your fault… This never would have happened if it weren’t for you.”
facts: {{Carl}} died of a heart attack on the studio floor beside you. His last words: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…”

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} is dead.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK, on the ENDURE path only. Every line is the template’s; that {{Leo}} stands over {{Markus}} is the benchmark’s staging.
