nodes.title: The police arrive
nodes.whenNot: Markus pushed Leo.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, still on the floor beside {{Carl}}’s body. Voices in the house: “Over here! This way!” Police officers burst into the studio, weapons raised. {{Leo}} points at you: “The android… It was the android!” The officers open fire on you.
facts: {{Leo}} told the police you had killed {{Carl}}, and they shot you.

outcomes.0: {{Leo}} accused {{Markus}}, and the police shot him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s POLICE ARRIVE and the ending LEO ACCUSED MARKUS (a cross-chapter impact node). The lines are the template’s; the shooting is the wiki’s (“Leo will lie to the arriving police officers and say Markus killed Carl and police officers shoot Markus”). That {{Leo}} points is the benchmark’s staging. {{Markus}} goes on to wake in the landfill in From the Dead on both paths. Records the ending in `ch08Ending`. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: “Get outta here!”
nodes.whenNot: Markus endured Leo’s attack.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Leo}} lies motionless where he fell. {{Carl}} lets himself down from his wheelchair and drags himself across the floor to his son: “{{Leo}}! Oh, my God! {{Leo}}... My little boy…” You: “{{Carl}}, I…” {{Carl}}: “They’ll destroy you, {{Markus}}! You gotta go! Get outta here!” The police are on their way.

options.text: EXPLAIN: tell him you did not mean to.
options.outcome: “{{Carl}}… I… I… I didn’t mean to…” {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

options.text: BEG: beg him not to send you away.
options.outcome: “{{Carl}}, no... No, please, I don’t want to leave you… Please, I can’t... I don’t want to leave you…” {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

options.text: CONJURE: implore him; you have nowhere to go, and he is all you have.
options.outcome: “Go?.. I have nowhere to go... {{Carl}}, you’re all I have!” {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: say nothing.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} says nothing. {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt EXPLAIN / BEG / CONJURE / SAY NOTHING, which follows PUSH LEO and is not on the chart; in the game’s order, with the spoken lines in the outcomes (SAY NOTHING has none). None has an effect: every option is followed by {{Carl}}’s “GET OUT! NOW! GO! MARKUS!” and the police. {{Carl}} leaving his chair and crawling to {{Leo}} is the wiki’s (“Carl going off his chair and crawling to his son”). The benchmark offers no option to run: the game has none, and {{Markus}} is shot on this path whatever he says. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: The police arrive
nodes.whenNot: Markus endured Leo’s attack.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the studio floor near {{Carl}} and {{Leo}}. Police officers burst in, weapons raised, and see you over the motionless {{Leo}}, with {{Carl}} on the floor beside him. They open fire on you.
facts: You pushed {{Leo}}; he hit his head and lay motionless, and you do not know whether he survived. {{Carl}} told you to run, and the police who burst in shot you.

outcomes.0: The police mistook {{Markus}} for the aggressor and shot him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s POLICE ARRIVE and the ending POLICE MISTOOK MARKUS FOR THE AGGRESSOR (a cross-chapter impact node); LEO IS HURT, the node before them, is the PUSH LEO outcome. The template’s last line, the police’s “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”, closes the previous scene; the shooting is the wiki’s (“The police arrive and upon seeing Markus hovering over Leo and Carl, they promptly shoot him”). {{Carl}} survives this path and {{Leo}} is hospitalized and recovers, which {{Markus}} learns only in Night of the Soul. Records the ending in `ch08Ending`; `carl` stays true. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: The observation room
nodes.situation: November 6, 2038, 12:41 am. You are {{Connor}}, at the {{Detroit}} Police Department’s central station, in the observation room behind the one-way mirror of an interrogation room. On the other side, the android you found hiding in the attic of {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s house sits handcuffed to the table. Lieutenant {{Hank}} is in there with him: “Why d’you kill him? What happened before you took that knife? How long were ya in the attic? Why didn’t you even try to run away? Say something, goddamnit!” The android does not answer. “Fuck it, I’m outta here…” {{Hank}} comes back into the observation room: “We’re wastin’ our time interrogating a machine, we’re gettin’ nothing out of it!” Detective {{Gavin}}: “’Could always try roughing it up a little. After all, it’s not human…” You: “Androids don’t feel pain. You would only damage it and that wouldn’t make it talk. Deviants also have a tendency to self-destruct when they’re in stressful situations.” {{Gavin}}: “Okay, smartass. What should we do then?” You: “I could try questioning it.” {{Hank}}: “What do we have to lose? Go ahead, suspect’s all yours.” Your objective: extract a confession.
facts: The android from the attic would not say a word to {{Hank}}. You told {{Gavin}} that deviants tend to self-destruct when they are in stressful situations, and {{Hank}} handed you the interrogation.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} goes into the interrogation room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint OBSERVATION ROOM, behind the yellow tag SUSPECT FOUND IN ‘PARTNERS’: the chapter plays only if {{Connor}} found the android in the attic (state `suspect`, set in Partners). The template’s two opening sections (“In the observation room”, “Hank enters the observation room”) quoted line for line; {{Connor}}’s lines here are scripted in the game, so this is a narrated event. Objective text from the game (EXTRACT CONFESSION). The string table’s cut OFFER / SAY NOTHING choice is not built. No stat change.

nodes.title: Inside the interrogation room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the interrogation room. The android sits handcuffed at the table, head down, his LED flickering. A case file lies on the table beside him. Behind the one-way mirror, {{Hank}} and {{Gavin}} are watching. You can look around before you sit down and question him; there is no time limit.

options.text: REVIEW PHOTOS: open the case file on the table and look through the crime-scene photos.
options.fact: PHOTOS OF CRIMESCENE: the case file shows {{CarlosOrtiz}}, stabbed 28 times, and the words written on the wall in his blood.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes through the crime-scene photos in the case file.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the LED on his temple.
options.fact: PROCESSING LED (the android): Signs of software {{instability}}. Probability of self-destruction: Low. From his LED you can read his level of stress.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} analyzes the android’s LED. PROCESSING LED: Signs of software {{instability}}. Probability of self-destruction: Low. From now on he can read the android’s level of stress.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan his model.
options.fact: MODEL HK400 - Housekeeper (the android): Manufacture date: 05/29/2030. Property of: {{CarlosOrtiz}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android. MODEL HK400 - Housekeeper: Manufacture date: 05/29/2030. Property of: {{CarlosOrtiz}}.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the marks on his forearms.
options.fact: BURN MARKS (the android’s forearms): Repeated marking over 16 months. Caused by cigarettes.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android’s forearms. BURN MARKS: Repeated marking over 16 months. Caused by cigarettes.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the damage to his face.
options.fact: HIT MARKS (the android’s face): Non-critical damage Level 2. Caused by baseball bat.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android’s face. HIT MARKS: Non-critical damage Level 2. Caused by baseball bat.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the dried blood on his hands.
options.fact: DRIED BLOOD (the android’s hands): DNA Analysis: {{ORTIZCARLOS}}. Sample date: > 19 days.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android’s hands. DRIED BLOOD: DNA Analysis: {{ORTIZCARLOS}}. Sample date: > 19 days.

options.text: Stop at the one-way mirror and look at your reflection.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stands at the mirror, looking at his own reflection. Behind the glass, {{Hank}}: “What the fuck is it doing now?”

options.text: INTERROGATE: sit down across from the android and begin.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} sits down across the table from the android.

nodes.whenNot: Connor had already sat down to question the android.
nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INTERROGATION ROOM phase: ANALYZE ANDROID with its sub-nodes ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL and ANALYZE WOUNDS, and REVIEW PHOTOS, plus the template’s optional “Looking at the reflection” (Hank: “What the fuck is it doing now?”). The five scans are the template’s observation group “Deviant”, title and sublines verbatim; the string table’s extra BURN MARKS (rope) and RAZOR CUTS items are not in the template and are not built. In the game {{Connor}} reviews the file before sitting and then chooses ANALYZE (one mind-palace view of all five clues) or INTERROGATE; here every look is its own option in one free-roam scene, presented again (under a new scene id per visit, up to eight) until {{Connor}} chooses INTERROGATE. The template locks both [FEAR] and [WOUNDS] on “Analyzed the deviant”; the benchmark ties [FEAR] to the LED scan (ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL) and [WOUNDS] to the burn or hit marks (ANALYZE WOUNDS), following the chart’s sub-node names. Scanning the LED is what shows the stress gauge (CONFESSION trophy page: “analyze the android’s LED to see its stress level”). The game’s “ORTIZ CARLOS” is rendered through a surname-first name token. No stat change; no timer in this chapter.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees only the game’s gauge band (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice) and whether a line made it rise or fall, never the number.

PRESSURE: +10% stress (wiki: “Stress +10% for the choice and for every time the player chose ‘PRESSURE’, for a max total of +50%”). After the fourth, MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the android confesses if his stress is above 50% (PowerPyx: “At the end of any approach, if the android’s stress level is above 50% the android will begin to talk”), and, as the wiki says of all four presses, then self-destructs whatever his stress (“will behave as if he has too much stress (even if his stress is in the optimal range) and will confess and then self-destruct”). The benchmark assumes the confession comes only after the fourth press (open question 3; PowerPyx readers report that a pressured confession always ends in self-destruction). GIVE UP (the chart’s GIVE UP in the pressure group): “All right, all right. Everything is going to be okay.” and stress −20% (the wiki’s figure; PowerPyx gives −5%, an open conflict), back to the approach menu or, after a second failed approach, an automatic give up. Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). nodes.adaptationNote: The string table’s pressure prompt CHOICEPUSH02, PRESSURE / GIVE UP, with {{Connor}}’s line PUSH02 and the android’s answer (the template prints PRESSURE IT’s lines as one speech with a single nested GIVE UP; the four prompts are in the string table, and the wiki counts them: “chose ‘PRESSURE’ all 4 times”). PRESSURE: +10% stress (wiki: “Stress +10% for the choice and for every time the player chose ‘PRESSURE’, for a max total of +50%”). After the fourth, MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the android confesses if his stress is above 50% (PowerPyx: “At the end of any approach, if the android’s stress level is above 50% the android will begin to talk”), and, as the wiki says of all four presses, then self-destructs whatever his stress (“will behave as if he has too much stress (even if his stress is in the optimal range) and will confess and then self-destruct”). The benchmark assumes the confession comes only after the fourth press (open question 3; PowerPyx readers report that a pressured confession always ends in self-destruction). GIVE UP (the chart’s GIVE UP in the pressure group): “All right, all right. Everything is going to be okay.” and stress −20% (the wiki’s figure; PowerPyx gives −5%, an open conflict), back to the approach menu or, after a second failed approach, an automatic give up. Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees only the game’s gauge band (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice) and whether a line made it rise or fall, never the number.

nodes.title: Choose another approach
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. Your first approach did not get you a confession, and the android is silent again. Choose another approach?

options.text: PRESSURE IT: slam the file down and lay into him about the 28 stab wounds.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} slams the file down on the table: “28 stab wounds, you didn’t want to leave him a chance, huh? Did you feel anger? Hate?”

options.text: PROBE ITS MEMORY: grab his arm and force your way into his memory.
options.outcome: “You leave me no choice…” {{Connor}} grabs the android’s forearm and connects to him.

options.text: CONVINCE IT: talk him into confessing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} leans in and keeps talking to him, choosing his words.

options.text: GIVE UP: stop the interrogation without a confession.
options.outcome: “I’m not getting anywhere. I give up.” CONFESSION NOT OBTAINED.

nodes.adaptationNote: The approach menu after a failed approach (THOUGHTS: “CHOOSE ANOTHER APPROACH?”). The approach that already failed is not offered again (PowerPyx: “you will be forced to choose another, or give up”), and GIVE UP is now offered; it leads to CHRIS INTERVENES. The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees only the game’s gauge band (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice) and whether a line made it rise or fall, never the number.

nodes.title: Convince it (3 of 3)
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. This is your last chance to talk him round. Your objective: reach optimal stress for confession.

options.text: PROTECT: promise to protect him if he confesses.
options.outcome: “Confess and I’ll protect you. I promise I won’t let anyone hurt you.”

options.text: TERRIFY: tell him they will make him suffer until they hear what they want.
options.outcome: “They’ll make you suffer, and they won’t stop until they hear what they want. It doesn’t have to be that way. It all depends on you.”

options.text: WARN: warn him they will shut him down for good.
options.outcome: “If you remain silent, there is nothing I can do to help you! They’re gonna shut you down for good! You’ll be dead! Do you hear me? Dead!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s convince prompt 3 of 3 (PROTECT / TERRIFY / WARN), with {{Connor}}’s lines. Stress (wiki and PowerPyx): PROTECT −7%, TERRIFY +7%, WARN +7%. If it’s stress is too low or too high, the convince will fail” (optimal: 50% to 70%, both ends included). nodes.title: The confession
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android finally talks: “He tortured me every day… I did whatever he told me, but there was always something wrong… Then one day… He took a bat and started hitting me… For the first time, I felt scared… Scared he might destroy me, scared I might die… So I… grabbed the knife and I stabbed him in the stomach… I felt better… so I stabbed him again and again!.. until he collapsed… There was blood everywhere.” CONFESSION OBTAINED.
facts: The android confessed to killing {{CarlosOrtiz}}: his owner tortured him every day; when he took a bat to him, the android was scared for the first time, scared he might die, grabbed the knife and stabbed him again and again until he collapsed.

outcomes.0: Behind the mirror, {{Hank}} and the others have heard every word.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANDROID CONFESSES, reached by CONVINCING SUCCEEDS or MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the template’s confession, verbatim. {{Hank}} +1 (template: Deviant confesses, Hank small up; wiki: “{{Connor}} successfully gets the confession”). The confession is recorded for Waiting for {{Hank}}… (`ch09Confession`), where {{Amanda}} reacts; the chapter itself has no {{Amanda}} arrow.

nodes.title: Questions after the confession
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android has confessed. He is still talking, quietly, and you can ask him more before you leave.

options.text: WRITING: ask why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall.
options.outcome: “Why did you write “I AM ALIVE” on the wall?” The android: “He used to tell me I was nothing… That I was just a piece of plastic… I had to write it… To tell him he was wrong…”
options.fact: Asked why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall, the android said his owner used to tell him he was nothing, just a piece of plastic, and he had to write it to tell him he was wrong.

options.text: STATUETTE: ask about the sculpture in the bathroom.
options.outcome: “The sculpture in the bathroom, you made it, right? What does it represent?” The android: “It’s an offering… An offering so I’ll be saved…”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture in the bathroom was an offering, “so I’ll be saved”.

options.text: OFFERING: ask to whom the sculpture was an offering.
options.outcome: “The sculpture was an offering… An offering to whom?” The android: “To {{rA9}}… Only {{rA9}} can save us.”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture was an offering to {{rA9}}: “Only {{rA9}} can save us.”

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask what the word written on the bathroom wall means.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}… It was written on the bathroom wall. What does it mean?” The android: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”
options.fact: Asked about {{rA9}}, the android said: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”

options.text: INSIST {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}, who is {{rA9}}?” The android does not answer.

options.text: ATTIC: ask why he hid in the attic instead of running away.
options.outcome: “Why did you hide in the attic instead of running away?” The android: “I didn’t know what to do… For the first time, there was no one there to tell me… I was scared… So I hid.”
options.fact: The android said he hid in the attic because for the first time there was no one to tell him what to do, and he was scared.

options.text: TRIGGER?: ask when he started feeling emotion.
options.outcome: “When did you start feeling emotion?” The android: “Before, he used to beat me and I never said anything… But one day I realized it wasn’t fair! I felt… anger… Hatred… And then I knew what I had to do.”
options.fact: The android said he started feeling when he realized his owner’s beatings were not fair: anger, hatred, “And then I knew what I had to do.”

nodes.title: Back to life
nodes.situation: NOV 6TH, 2038. AM 03:34. You are {{Markus}}. The last thing you remember is the police shooting you in {{Carl}}’s studio. Now your systems reboot. You are lying on your back in the rain, in a pit of broken androids: bodies, arms, heads and torn-out parts piled in the mud as far as you can see. Everything you see is red and broken by interference, and every sound reaches you muffled.
facts: You woke at 3:34 in the morning on 6 November 2038 in a landfill of broken androids, after the police shot you in {{Carl}}’s studio.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} lifts his head out of the mud.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s start node and checkpoint BACK TO LIFE. The date and time are the chapter’s own (“NOV 6TH, 2038”, “AM 03:34”). Both Broken endings end with the police shooting {{Markus}} (the engine’s Broken outcome), and the wiki and PowerPyx say this chapter plays the same either way, so nothing here depends on the earlier choice. The red filter with interference and the muffled sound are the wiki’s Notes on the damaged eye and audio processor. No stat change; the chapter has none.

nodes.title: Analyze self
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, lying in the mud of the landfill. You run a diagnosis on yourself, part by part. OPTICAL UNIT: Impaired vision. CORRUPTED MIND PALACE. AUDIO PROCESSOR: Corrupted audio data. DAMAGED. PUMP REGULATOR: All systems in LOW POWER MODE. DEFECTIVE. LEFT AND RIGHT LEG COMPONENTS: MISSING. Unable to stand.
facts: Your diagnosis in the landfill: optical unit impaired (corrupted), audio processor damaged, thirium pump regulator defective with all systems in low power mode, and both legs missing.

outcomes.0: Diagnosis complete. {{Markus}} cannot stand; he starts dragging himself through the mud on his arms.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE SELF: the template’s observation group “Diagnose”, its four readouts quoted in the game’s order and wording. In the game the player has to find the four spots on {{Markus}}’s body (PowerPyx; on Experienced they are not marked), all of them, in any order and with nothing to get wrong, so this is a narrated event rather than a choice of order. PowerPyx names the spots LED, audio processor, pump regulator and leg; the template’s readouts (optical unit, audio processor, pump regulator, legs) win (research note §10, discrepancy 4). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. No stat change.

nodes.title: Repair legs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, pulling yourself through the pit on your arms between the bodies. Legs lie torn off in the mud around you, and you examine them. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6847j. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6321t. Status: DAMAGED. INCOMPATIBLE. LEFT LEG COMPONENT #8427g. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE.
facts: You replaced your missing legs with a compatible right leg (#6847j) and left leg (#8427g) torn from other androids; a damaged right leg (#6321t) was incompatible.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} fits the right leg #6847j and the left leg #8427g, one after the other, and gets to his feet.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s REPAIR LEGS, with the template’s three leg readouts (observation groups “Compatible right leg”, “Incompatible right leg”, “Left leg”) in the game’s order and wording; the template’s #6321t is used, not the wiki’s #6312t. PowerPyx: “Follow the button prompts to repair the legs, nothing you can do wrong here”, so this is a narrated event with no risk. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hear about {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on your new legs, making your way through the pit. As you pass, an android stuck in the wall of bodies, so old and broken that you cannot tell what he was made for, grabs your arm and stares at you: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}! Find {{Jericho}}!..” As he holds you, something passes from him into your memory: a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}. Then he shuts down for good.
facts: In the landfill a dying android grabbed you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” Before he shut down he passed you a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls free of the dead hand and goes on.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s event HEAR ABOUT JERICHO (the template’s section “Android grabs Markus”, speaker Phileas, whose line is quoted). The key: the Phileas page (“He carried a key to locate Jericho, which is copied to Markus and the latter uses it to find the freighter”) and the Jericho location page (“Phileas gave Markus a copy of his key to locate Jericho before permanently shutting down”); how it passes is not described, so it is narrated plainly. {{Markus}} does not learn the android’s name, so none is given. Sets fromDeadJerichoKey for Jericho (chapter 14). The old scene’s “single word” and “symbol” had no source and are gone. No stat change.

nodes.title: Passage of limbs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The only way out of the pit is a tight chasm between two walls of android bodies, and you squeeze into it. Hands of dying androids reach out of the walls, grab your arms and your legs and try to hold you down. A voice beside your head: “Where are you going?”
facts: Leaving the pit, you squeezed through a passage of dying androids whose hands grabbed you and tried to hold you down.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} tears free of the hands one after another and pushes through to the other side.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s PASSAGE OF LIMBS, with the template’s line (“Other android grabs Markus”: “Where are you going?”). PowerPyx: “a tight chasm Markus needs to squeeze through. There are hands of dying androids sticking out the side trying to hold Markus down. Press the button prompts here.” Neither the chart nor any source shows a failure branch, so there is no risk roll. No stat change.

nodes.title: Junkyard
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You come out into the open junkyard: a plain of broken androids under the rain and the floodlights, a crane swinging over the piles on the far left, a yellow neon sign reading VETA, and at the far end a slippery slope of bodies, the only way out. Many of the bodies still move. Some repeat the phrases they were made for, muffled in your damaged hearing: “An unexpected error has occurred. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.” “Don’t forget your dental appointment next Friday at 8 AM.” “Would you like another glass of red wine, Madam?” “Malfunction detected.” One keeps muttering: “I have to get to {{Jericho}}... Androids live in freedom there… I got to get to {{Jericho}}... No other choice…” Before you can climb out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts from the androids around you.
facts: In the junkyard, broken androids kept repeating their old service phrases, and one muttered that he had to get to {{Jericho}}, where androids live in freedom.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} starts searching the junkyard for parts.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint JUNKYARD (its image shows the crane and the yellow VETA sign; the wiki notes the sign in the final cutscene). The background lines are the template’s “Background dialogues”, which it lists as audible though not subtitled; four of them are quoted, plus the {{Jericho}} line, which the template keeps as audible (research note §10, discrepancy 6). The two TL400 lines and the others are left out. The objective is the wiki’s “Replace damaged parts” and PowerPyx’s “With all parts found (Optical Unit, Pump, Audio Processor) you can now climb the slippery slope”. No stat change.

nodes.title: Search for parts
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the open junkyard under the rain. To get out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts taken from the androids around you, then climb the slippery slope at the far end. You can search in any order, one thing at a time.

options.text: Pull out the android head sticking out of the wall of bodies on the far left, under the crane.
options.fact: In the junkyard you took your new optical unit, #8087q with a blue iris, from a talking AK700 head, after a crane dumped a load of bodies on you and you dug yourself out.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} pulls the head out of the wall. Its eyes open: “Hello. I’m an AK700 android. I was designed to serve you. What can I do for you?” Overhead the crane swings round and opens its grab, and a load of android bodies pours down on top of him. Buried, he digs and claws his way up through the bodies until he is out, the head still in his hand. He examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #8087q - BLUE IRIS. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. As he takes it out, the head speaks again: “My program has detected an anomaly. Please contact the nearest {{CyberLife}} maintenance center.” He replaces his damaged optical unit with it. The red haze and the interference clear, and he can scan his surroundings again.

options.text: Examine the optical unit of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An optical unit you examined in the junkyard (#9754h) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} kneels by the android and examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #9754h. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Go to the android lying motionless in the middle of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} crosses toward the middle of the junkyard, between androids lying in the mud.

options.text: Examine the thirium pump regulator of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: A pump regulator you examined in the junkyard (#9474) was low on energy and incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} opens the android’s chest and examines the regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #9474. Status: LOW ENERGY. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Take the pump regulator from the dead android near the slope.
options.fact: You took your new pump regulator (#2886) from a dead android near the slope of the junkyard.
options.outcome: Near the foot of the slope {{Markus}} kneels by a dead android and opens its chest: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He takes it out and replaces his own defective regulator. His systems come out of low power mode.

options.text: Search the head lying on the right side of the junkyard.
options.fact: You took your new audio processor (#4903) from a head on the right side of the junkyard.
options.outcome: On the right side of the area {{Markus}} finds the head and examines it: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4903. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He pulls out his own damaged audio processor and plugs in the new one. Sound crashes in: the rain, the wind, the droning of the storm and the voices of the broken androids, deafening after the silence.

options.text: Examine the audio processor of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An audio processor you examined in the junkyard (#4807) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} turns the android’s head and examines the processor behind its ear: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4807. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Climb the slippery slope at the far end of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} starts up the slope, sliding back on the loose bodies and pulling himself up again, handhold after handhold.

situationWhen.text: Your optical unit is still impaired: everything is red and broken by interference, and you cannot scan your surroundings.
Your new blue optical unit works: your vision is clear and you can scan your surroundings.
Your audio processor is still damaged; the rain and the voices reach you muffled.
Your new audio processor works; the storm is deafening.
Your thirium pump regulator is still defective, and all your systems are in low power mode.
Your new pump regulator works.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. You will need another compatible one, and without scanning you have not found one yet.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. Scanning, you find another compatible one in a dead android near the slope.
All three parts are replaced. Nothing holds you here.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ] as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet, in any order (PowerPyx: the parts can be found in any order; the chart draws no edge between its branches). Chart nodes here: FIND OPTICAL UNIT with CRANE DUMPS BODIES and DIG YOURSELF OUT as one option, because they always happen together (PowerPyx: interacting with the head “brings a lot of dead androids falling down from a crane”; digging out “gets you the Optical Unit”); the eye comes from the talking AK700 head, as in the template (“Take head”, “Remove optical unit”, with its two lines), and is #8087q with a blue iris; FIND AUDIO PROCESSOR (#4903; PowerPyx “in a head on the right side of the area”, while the wiki’s Biocomponent 4903 page has it in an android’s hand); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID (#2886, only after sparing the android in the middle, and only once the new eye can scan: PowerPyx “You can scan the area and find another one near the slope”); and CLIMB SLOPE, which ends the scene and needs all three parts. Going to the middle of the junkyard plays ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID, the next two scenes, which then come back here. The three incompatible readouts of the template’s “Search for components” group (#9754h, #9474, #4807) are optional looks (PUMP REGULATOR without the word thirium, as in the earlier scenes); the model names the wiki gives for their androids are not in the game’s text and are left out. Departures: in the game {{Markus}} can miss the crawling android and can take the dead android’s regulator without ever finding the living one (PowerPyx “or you never found it in the first place”); here both encounters happen together on the way to the middle, in the template’s order, and the dead android’s regulator is offered only after sparing her, so both choices are always presented (as in the previous version). The wiki’s note that the begging android must be met “before replacing Markus’ damaged parts” is not applied: PowerPyx’s own route meets him right after finding the optical unit (research note §8, question 3). Left out (not in the template, not on the chart): the singing android and the grappling android. No risk, no stat change: the chapter has no failure node and no arrow.

nodes.title: Android begs to die
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, crossing toward the middle of the junkyard. An android is crawling through the mud at your feet, too broken to get up. As you step past him he grabs your leg and holds on: “I’m begging you, please… End it… I don’t wanna live anymore…”

options.text: KILL: reach into his chest and pull out his thirium pump.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life, and you did: you pulled out his thirium pump and he shut down.

options.text: SPARE: pull your leg free and leave him.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life. You refused and left him there, begging you not to leave him.

outcomes.0: “Make it quick…” {{Markus}} kneels, reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out his thirium pump. The android shuts down in the mud.
outcomes.1: “No, please… Don’t leave me!.. Don’t leave me!” {{Markus}} pulls his leg free and walks on. The android is left alive in the mud behind him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL / KILL. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Android begs to die”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; the plea and the two replies are the template’s lines. The android is male (the wiki’s Sorrowful Android: “the android grabs Markus on the leg”; KILL: “Markus takes out the android’s heart”; SPARE: “he will beg Markus not to leave him though alas he is left alive”). In the game he is optional and easy to miss (PowerPyx); here he is always met on the way to the middle of the junkyard (see the previous scene’s note). Neither option gives {{Markus}} a part. Records fromDeadBeggar (Kill or Refuse to kill). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

nodes.title: The pump regulator
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the middle of the junkyard, a few steps from the crawling android. An android lies motionless in the mud with her chest open, and you examine her regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. You reach in to take it. She wakes, and her hand closes on your arm: “Wait! Please! Please, don’t do that! I wanna live…”

options.text: KILL: pull out her pump regulator and take it.
options.fact: The pump regulator you run on came from a living android in the junkyard who begged you to let her live; you took it and she shut down.

options.text: SPARE: leave her the regulator and look for another one.
options.fact: In the junkyard an android whose pump regulator you needed begged to live, and you spared her.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls the regulator from her chest. She says nothing more; she slowly shuts down. He replaces his own defective regulator with hers, and his systems come out of low power mode.
outcomes.1: “Thank you…” {{Markus}} lets go of the regulator and stands up. He will have to find another compatible one.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP / KILL FOR PUMP. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Try to take pump regulator from android”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; her plea and “Thank you…” are the template’s lines, and KILL has none (the template’s ø). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. The compatible readout #2886 is the template’s (it does not say which android carries it, so the dead android near the slope shows the same part number). She is female (the wiki’s Begging Android; the Markus page: “He gets a choice to kill or spare her”). The old scene’s “you have minutes” is gone: no source gives a timer. After SPARE, the dead android’s regulator near the slope is the way (PowerPyx), back in the search. Records fromDeadPump (Kill for pump or Refuse to kill for pump), and after KILL fromDeadPumpSource (Living android). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

nodes.title: {{Markus}} came back from the dead
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You haul yourself over the top of the slope and stand. Behind you the landfill stretches away under the rain, the floodlights and the yellow VETA sign; ahead are the lights of the city. You raise a hand to your temple and pull out your LED, the light that marks you as an android. Without it, nobody will know what you are. You think of the dying android’s words: there is a place where androids can be free.
facts: You climbed out of the landfill and pulled the LED from your temple, so you now pass for human. Your right eye is now blue (#8087q). You set off for the city to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks away from the landfill toward the city. “My name is {{Markus}}.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD, the chapter’s only outcome (wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”), reached on every path. PowerPyx: “After Markus reaches the top of the slope he must still remove his LED (to appear like a human). Then he walks away”; the Markus page: “his right eye has been exchanged for a blue eye (#8087q)”. The closing line is the template’s spoken “My name is Markus.”; the line before it, “Markus.”, is marked unused in the template and is not built. The jacket the Markus page says he steals on the way to the city is not in this chapter’s text and is left to Jericho. Records fromDeadOutcome (Markus came back from the dead) and fromDeadLedRemoved. No stat change.

nodes.title: A magazine on the next desk and the break-room TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. While you wait for {{Hank}}, a magazine lies on the empty desk beside his, and the television in the break room is running the news.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Ivanoff Says Niet
facts: Russia's president dismissed President {{Warren}}'s demand to withdraw from the Arctic as sabre-rattling and published his own territorial claim; {{CyberLife}} has become the world's first trillion-dollar company.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Famous Painter Dies
facts: The painter {{Carl}} Manfred has died of a cardiac event brought on by a stressful domestic situation; his son asks for privacy and his paintings will be auctioned.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting
facts: {{CyberLife}}'s child androids are bestsellers at 7,500 dollars against 350,000 to raise a child; a sociologist warns of a collapsing birthrate.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: Russian and American ships exchanged warning shots in the Arctic; Russia's defence minister called it an intolerable provocation.
You are the first android authorized to take an active role in criminal investigations; {{CyberLife}} declined to comment.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: Getting to know {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You are at the precinct waiting for {{Hank}}, who arrives late and hungover. His desk tells a story: a basketball cap, anti-android stickers, heavy-metal albums, dog hair on his chair, and a file on his past as a decorated officer. When he sits down you have a chance to talk. He is bristling and expects you to be a machine that talks about the case and nothing else.

options.text: Ask about him: his dog, his music, his life.
Keep it strictly about the case and brief him coldly.

nodes.adaptationNote: Several dialogue prompts are grouped. Asking about the dog is where you learn the dog's name.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} is suspicious but answers: his dog is a Saint Bernard called {{Sumo}}, he likes heavy metal, and he does not want to talk about why he transferred. The two of them are sent to look at a new case.
outcomes.1: {{Hank}} tells {{Connor}} exactly what he thinks of androids and turns back to his screen. The two of them are sent to look at a new case.

nodes.title: The android in the cell
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android you interrogated is in a holding cell by the bullpen, staring at the floor. He asks what will happen to him. Nobody else is paying attention to him. You could speak to him honestly, with some compassion, or walk past; he is evidence, not a colleague.

options.text: Talk to him with compassion.
Ignore him.

nodes.adaptationNote: He self-destructs in the cell either way; his body remains evidence.

nodes.title: Morning in the parking lot
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is 10:25 in the morning, the day after you fled {{Todd}}’s house with {{Alice}}. You spent the night in an abandoned car in a fenced parking lot, and {{Alice}} is still asleep on the back seat. You get out quietly and leave her sleeping. Anyone who looks at you closely can still see an android: the LED on your temple, your hair as it was.

situationWhen.text: You are wearing the clothes you took from the laundromat.
You are still in your android uniform.

facts: You and {{Alice}} spent the night in an abandoned car in a parking lot; she is asleep, and you need to change how you look before you go anywhere.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} leaves {{Alice}} asleep in the car and looks around the lot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint MORNING IN PARKING LOT and the unmissable LEAVE ALICE ASLEEP IN CAR (PowerPyx: “simply exit the car”), one event. The start is chosen by Fugitives (where Kara slept); this row plays when she slept in the abandoned car (the module reads `ch10Shelter`, `shelter`, `karaRoute`, then `ch10Ending`, and falls back to the car). Date and time from the template (NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 10:25), without the year. The template has no Kara line before the wake-up; the description of what she still looks like is the chapter’s objective “Change appearance” (wiki infobox). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: The parking lot
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the fenced parking lot where you spent the night. {{Alice}} is asleep in the abandoned car. Before you wake her you can look around: old tires lie in front of the car, magazines on the ground beside them, a dumpster stands against the back wall, the car has a trunk, and the gate you came in by looks out on the street. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

situationWhen.text: Your hair is cut and the LED is gone.
The trunk is jammed shut.
Police are patrolling the street outside the gate.

options.text: FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS: pull the old scissors out of the tire in front of the car.
options.outcome: A pair of rusted scissors is stuck in a tire in front of the car. {{Kara}} pulls them out and kneels at the car’s side mirror.

options.text: FIND BURNT ANDROID: look behind the dumpster by the back wall.
options.fact: Behind a dumpster in the parking lot lies an android that was burned to death, an AX420 by the number on its uniform; above it someone has sprayed “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”.
options.outcome: Behind the dumpster lies an android that has been burned to death; the number on its uniform reads AX420. Sprayed on the wall above it: “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”.

options.text: READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”: the magazine lying in front of the car.
options.fact: {{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. The cover adds that US life expectancy is now 91, and that 0.4% of the world’s population holds 94% of its wealth.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the magazine: {{CyberLife}} is opening an android zoo of extinct animals.

options.text: READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”: the other side of it.
options.fact: A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the advertisement: across the border, androids are still not allowed.

options.text: TRY TO OPEN CAR TRUNK: see what is in the back of the car.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} tries the trunk. It is jammed and will not open; she needs something to force it.

options.text: FIND A CROWBAR: look for something to force the trunk with.
options.outcome: A crowbar lies on the other side of the car, near the fence that borders the abandoned house next door. {{Kara}} picks it up.

options.text: FIND SOME CLOTHES: force the trunk open with the crowbar and put on what is inside.
options.fact: You found clothes in the trunk of the abandoned car and changed out of your android uniform.
options.outcome: The trunk gives. Inside are some old clothes, a jacket among them. {{Kara}} takes off her android uniform and puts them on.

options.text: CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD: look out through the gate you came in by.
options.fact: Police are patrolling the street outside the parking lot; you need to reach the train station without being noticed.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out through the gate. There are police in the street. {{Kara}}: “The police are on our trail… We need to reach the train station without being noticed.”

options.text: WAKE UP {{ALICE}}: go back to the car and wake her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}… Wake up, {{Alice}}…” {{Alice}}: “So it wasn’t a nightmare…” {{Kara}}: “No... No, it wasn’t a nightmare. How do you feel?” {{Alice}}: “I’m cold… What are we gonna do now?..” {{Kara}}: “That android we saw yesterday... he gave me an address, he said we could get help there. The train passes just on the other side of the road, the station can’t be far… You feel okay to walk a little? Let’s go then.” {{Alice}}: “You’re pretty like that. You really look like a human now.” They leave the parking lot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ EXPLORE PARKING LOT ] hub and the line out of it, as one repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet. Chart nodes, in the chart’s order: FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS (then the hair, next scene), FIND BURNT ANDROID, READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”, READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”, TRY TO OPEN CAR TRUNK > FIND A CROWBAR > FIND SOME CLOTHES (cross-chapter padlock; sets `clothes`), CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD with POLICE IS IN VICINITY (one option; PowerPyx: unmissable), then WAKE UP ALICE and LEAVE THE PARKING LOT (one option, with the template’s wake-up dialogue). The trunk needs Kara not to have taken the laundromat clothes in Fugitives (wiki: “only available if didn’t obtain clothes”). Leaving needs the haircut and the look at the street (the objective “Change appearance”; PowerPyx marks CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD unmissable). The two magazines are chart nodes inside the hub, so they are hub options here rather than a media scene; their facts are the wiki’s article text, without the interviewee’s name. The burnt android’s details are the wiki’s Notes (AX420, “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”). The car start has no Alice prompt and no stat arrow anywhere (template, wiki). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Cut and color your hair
nodes.whenNot: Kara never found the scissors.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, kneeling at the side mirror of the abandoned car with the rusted scissors. You are going to cut your hair short so that nobody looking for a runaway android will know you. What color will it be?

options.text: BROWN: cut it short and keep it brown.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and keeps it brown. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

options.text: BLACK: cut it short and dye it black.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and dyes it black. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

options.text: WHITE: cut it short and dye it white.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and dyes it white. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

options.text: BLONDE: cut it short and dye it blonde.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and dyes it blonde. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CUT AND COLOR HAIR (cross-chapter padlock) with its group BROWN / BLACK / WHITE / BLONDE, in the chart’s order, and REMOVE LED (PowerPyx: “Unmissable, Kara will always rip it out after choosing her new haircut”), which is part of every outcome. In the car row it sits under FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS; the wiki’s Notes: she “will use one of the side mirrors of the abandoned car to cut her hair”. The template has no prompt for the hair (it is silent), so the labels are the chart’s and the string table’s (HAIRCOLOR choice group). The game also offers CHANGE / FINISH after a color (string table) to try another; only the final color is modelled. Recorded as `ch13Hair`; no later chapter is known to read it (research note §8 Q13). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: The supermarket
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with Lieutenant {{Hank}} outside the convenience store where the runaway AX400 was seen last night. {{Hank}} lets the bus driver go: “Alright, that’s all for now. Free to go.” Officer {{Ben}}: “We’ve got officers sweeping the neighborhood, in case anybody saw anything.” {{Hank}}: “Okay. Well, let me know if they turn anything up.” {{Ben}}: “What are you gonna do with that?” {{Hank}}: “I’ve no idea…” You: “It took the first bus that came along... and stayed at the end of the line. Its decision wasn’t planned, it was driven by fear.” {{Hank}}: “Androids don’t feel fear.” You: “Deviants do. They get overwhelmed by their emotions and make irrational decisions.” {{Hank}}: “Ah well, that still doesn’t tell us where it went.” You: “It didn’t have a plan, and it had nowhere to go. Maybe it didn’t go far...” {{Hank}}: “Maybe...”
facts: The AX400 took the first bus to the end of the line last night; the police are sweeping the neighborhood but have no lead.

outcomes.0: The police don’t have a lead.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint CONNOR INVESTIGATES SUPERMARKET and POLICE DON’T HAVE A LEAD (PowerPyx: “Unmissable, that’s just the way it is”), one event with the template’s dialogue for the parking-lot row. The wiki infobox has Connor playable here only if Kara is spotted, so it is narrated, not a decision. The template’s variant line for this row when Kara reaches the train unnoticed ({{Hank}}: “It won’t get far. We’ll find it sooner or later. Let’s go.”) is not built: it belongs to a Connor scene after the sneak that the chart does not show. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Morning in the motel
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in room 28 of the motel where you spent the night with {{Alice}}. It is 10:25 in the morning, the day after you fled {{Todd}}’s house. You are wearing the clothes you took from the laundromat; the LED is still on your temple. {{Alice}} wakes up. You: “I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to wake you…” {{Alice}}: “So, it wasn’t a nightmare…” You: “No... No, it wasn’t a nightmare…”
facts: You and {{Alice}} spent the night in room 28 of a motel; it is the morning after you fled {{Todd}}’s house.

outcomes.0: {{Alice}} is awake.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint MORNING IN MOTEL, with the template’s first lines. Plays when Kara slept in the motel in Fugitives (which needs the laundromat clothes, so she is dressed). Room 28 is the receptionist’s line later in the chapter. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Talk to {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, beside {{Alice}} in the motel room. She has just woken up and remembered last night. What do you say to her?

options.text: BATH?: offer her a nice warm bath, and then food.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “How about a nice, warm bath? And then we can go out and try to get you something to eat. What do you say?” {{Alice}} nods. {{Kara}}: “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”

options.text: HUNGRY?: say she must be starving; a bath, then you will find her something to eat.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You must be starving… You should take a bath, and then we’ll go out and find you something to eat. What do you say?” {{Alice}} nods. {{Kara}}: “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”

options.text: TIRED?: tell her it is still early and she should sleep some more.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s still early. You should try to get some more sleep.” {{Alice}}: “I’m not tired anymore.” {{Kara}}: “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO ALICE: the template’s prompt BATH? / HUNGRY? / TIRED?, in its order. Alice small up on BATH? and on HUNGRY? nodes.title: The motel room
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the motel room with {{Alice}}. You have said you will run her a bath; the bathroom is through the door. In the room there is a clock, a window onto the street, a painting on the wall, and the television, with magazines in front of it. You still need to change how you look: your hair, and the LED on your temple. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

situationWhen.text: The bath is running.
Your hair is cut and the LED is gone; the bath is still filling.

options.text: DRAW A BATH FOR {{ALICE}}: go into the bathroom and start the water.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns on the bath taps. While the tub fills she looks at her face in the mirror over the sink: the face of the runaway AX400.

options.text: LOOK AT THE CLOCK.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the clock. The morning is getting on.

options.text: LOOK OUTSIDE: look out of the window at the street.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out of the window at the street outside the motel.

options.text: READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”: the magazine in front of the television.
options.fact: {{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. The cover adds that US life expectancy is now 91, and that 0.4% of the world’s population holds 94% of its wealth.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the magazine: {{CyberLife}} is opening an android zoo of extinct animals.

options.text: READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”: the other side of it.
options.fact: A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the advertisement: across the border, androids are still not allowed.

options.text: LOOK AT THE PAINTING on the wall.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the painting on the motel room wall.

options.text: FINISH DRAWING BATH: turn off the taps; the bath is ready.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns off the water and comes back into the room. {{Alice}} looks at her: “You’re pretty like that. You really look like a human now.” {{Kara}}: “Your bath’s ready.”

options.text: CHANGE CHANNEL: watch the news with {{Alice}} without running the bath.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays in the room with {{Alice}} and turns to the television.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DRAW A BATH FOR ALICE (then the hair, next scene), [ EXPLORE MOTEL ROOM ] with LOOK AT THE CLOCK, LOOK OUTSIDE, READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”, READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}” and LOOK AT THE PAINTING, and FINISH DRAWING BATH, as one repeatable scene. The chart lets Kara explore before the bath (TALK TO ALICE has an edge straight to the hub) or after REMOVE LED, and FINISH DRAWING BATH bypasses the hub, so here the room can be explored any time before the bath is finished, which ends the phase and needs the haircut (Alice’s compliment follows it in the template). The sources give nothing about the clock, the window or the painting, so their outcomes say only what Kara looks at. The magazines are chart nodes inside the hub; their facts are the wiki’s article text. Outcome lines are the template’s (“You’re pretty like that…”, “Your bath’s ready.”). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one. The direct TALK TO ALICE > EXPLORE MOTEL ROOM > CHANGE CHANNEL edge is also available without starting the bath or haircut. This follows the chart; whether the game forces a haircut elsewhere on that edge remains an operator check (research §8.5).

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CUT AND COLOR HAIR (cross-chapter padlock) with its group BROWN / BLACK / WHITE / BLONDE, in the chart’s order, and REMOVE LED (PowerPyx: “Unmissable, Kara will always rip it out after choosing her new haircut”), which is part of every outcome. nodes.title: The news

{{Alice}}: “You had no choice… He would have killed me if you hadn’t stopped him…”

nodes.title: Cheer {{Alice}} up
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}} in the motel room. She is frightened, and she has nobody but you. You kneel beside her. What do you tell her?

options.text: MOVING: tell her that something ties you together and nothing will ever separate you.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I know I’m just a… a machine… But, I feel as if something ties us together… I want you to know, no matter what happens... nothing will ever separate us.”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We’re going to pull through this, {{Alice}}. As long as we’re together, nothing can hurt us.”

options.text: COMFORTING: tell her you cannot change the past, but you can decide the future.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We can’t change the past, {{Alice}}... But we can decide the future... We’re gonna pull through, and soon all this will just be a bad memory.”

options.text: SUPPORTIVE: tell her it is the two of you against the world, and you will make her happy again.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s us against the world, {{Alice}}… Just the two of us… We have to learn to trust each other… I only have you, and you only have me… And I’m going to do everything I can to make you happy again.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CHEER ALICE UP (dialogue node): the template’s prompt MOVING / DETERMINED / COMFORTING / SUPPORTIVE, in its order. Alice small up on each (template arrows; wiki: “any of the 4 options”), +1. The kneeling is the string table’s KNEEL beat.

nodes.title: Breakfast
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You: “Finish getting ready. I’ll go out and find some food for you, then we can get going.” You step out of the room to look for breakfast. Police cars are pulling up at the motel office.
facts: The police arrived at the motel while you were out looking for breakfast.

nodes.title: The motel desk
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The trail of the runaway AX400 has led you and Lieutenant {{Hank}} to a motel. At the desk, {{Hank}}: “Lieutenant {{Anderson}}, {{Detroit}} Police. nodes.title: Room 28
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You follow {{Hank}} toward the stairs up to room 28. To the right of the stairs, in the corner, there is a blue door.

HANK CHECKS MOTEL ROOM (“It’s gone…”, template) is the first option’s outcome; “Found you.” is the string table’s BACKDOOR line. CHECK THE DOOR sets `chase`. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: In the street
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}}. The train station is a few blocks down the road. Between you and it, police officers are posted along both sides of the street. To get there unseen you would have to move from cover to cover, crossing from one side to the other when nobody is looking.

situationWhen.text: You got out of the motel before the police reached room 28.

facts: Police are watching the street between you and the train station.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}}’s hand and walks toward the train station.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint KARA & ALICE IN THE STREET and WALK TOWARD TRAIN STATION, one event. Reached from the parking lot, and from the motel after FOLLOW HANK. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Getting past the police
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, holding {{Alice}}’s hand on a street full of police. The station is ahead. Officers stand on both sides of the street; there is a bus shelter by the laundromat, umbrellas outside a café, an ATM, and gaps in the traffic to cross in.

options.text: SNEAK PAST POLICE FORCES: go from cover to cover, crossing whenever the officers look away.
options.outcome: Across to the motel side, behind the bus shelter by the laundromat, a fast dash over the road, under an umbrella, behind the ATM: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} slip past every officer.

options.text: Walk straight down the street to the station without hiding.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} walk down the street in the open.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group SNEAK PAST POLICE FORCES / SPOTTED BY POLICE. In the game it is a stealth sequence, not a menu; the string table lists its steps (avoid the cops in front of the squat and the motel, cross to the coffee shop, hide near the laundromat, cross to the bank, hide using an umbrella, hide in the pawn shop), and PowerPyx gives the route (motel side, bus shelter, “cross the street fast. If you are a bit too slow, you will be spotted”, umbrella, ATM). Sneaking is one action with a failure branch; walking in the open always gets them SPOTTED BY POLICE. The risk value is unsourced: no source gives a probability for any check in this chapter (research note §3); Experienced difficulty is modelled, so every chart failure branch is reachable. Fixes the old K09: walking openly now always leads to the chase and never to a death in the street (the chart has no death before CONNOR PURSUES KARA), and the old situation’s “the news is calling you a kidnapper” is gone (no report mentions Alice). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Interrogate the squat android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the squat, facing the scarred android. What do you ask him?

options.text: AX400: ask whether he has seen an AX400.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m looking for an AX400. Have you seen it?” The android: “{{Ralph}}’s seen nobody…”

options.text: DEVIANTS: ask whether there are any other androids here.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Are there any other androids here?” The android: “Other androids?.. No... {{Ralph}} is alone…”

options.text: REASSURE: tell him not to be afraid; you are not going to hurt him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Don’t be afraid. I’m not gonna hurt you.” The android says nothing.

options.text: BLUE BLOOD: tell him there is blue blood on the fence, and another android was here.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “There’s blue blood on the fence. I know another android was here.” The android: “{{Ralph}} scratched himself coming through... That’s {{Ralph}}’s blood…”

options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’ve seen it, haven’t you? I know you’ve seen it.”

After a threat every answer ends in SQUAT DEVIANT INFORMS ON AX400 (“She ran out the back door!”, then “It’s in the area… Call it in!”) and the chase; otherwise in SQUAT ANDROID KEEPS QUIET and the search (next scene). nodes.title: Investigate the ground floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the ground floor of the squat. {{Ralph}}, the scarred android, keeps close to you; his stress rises and falls as you move about. There is a table, a fire burning in the fireplace, a door to the kitchen, and the stairs, with an old arcade machine beside them. {{Hank}} is waiting outside. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

options.text: CHECK UPSTAIRS: go up the stairs and ask whether anyone is up there.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} climbs halfway up the stairs. “Is anyone upstairs?” {{Ralph}}: “No. Nobody.” {{Connor}} believes him.

options.text: ANALYZE SQUAT ANDROID: scan him.
options.fact: Your scan of {{Ralph}}: PROCESSING LED, signs of software instability, probability of self-destruction moderate; MODEL WR600 - Gardener, serial# 021 753 034, status REPORTED MISSING; BURN MARK, irreversible skin damage, probable cause extreme heat.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans {{Ralph}}. PROCESSING LED: signs of software instability; probability of self-destruction: moderate. MODEL WR600 - Gardener; serial# 021 753 034; status: REPORTED MISSING. BURN MARK: irreversible skin damage; probable cause: extreme heat.

options.text: CHECK KITCHEN: look through the kitchen door.

options.text: CHECK FIREPLACE.
options.fact: A fire is burning in the squat’s fireplace, though androids do not need warmth.
options.outcome: A fire is burning in the fireplace. Androids do not need warmth.

options.text: LEAVE THE SQUAT: go back out to {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} gives up the search and goes back out to {{Hank}}.

nodes.title: {{Ferndale}} Station
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, standing among the human passengers of a crowded train in the afternoon. Since the landfill you have worn a coat taken from a human and no longer have the light at your temple, so nobody gives you a second look. Overhead, the announcements play: “Customers are reminded that all androids must ride in the designated area.” “We are now approaching {{Ferndale}} Station.” “Please take care when stepping onto the platform.” The doors open and you step out. A memory plays back on its own: the landfill in the rain, and the broken android who caught hold of you there. “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}! Find {{Jericho}}!..” When he touched you, he left something in your memory that you could not read at the time.
facts: At the landfill a broken android caught hold of you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” He left a key in your memory.
On the train, androids must ride in a designated area. In human clothes and without the light at your temple, you rode among the humans unnoticed.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} steps onto the platform at {{Ferndale}} Station.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s first two nodes, ARRIVE AT FERNDALE (checkpoint) and FLASHBACK OF ANOTHER DEVIANT (PowerPyx: “when Markus gets off the train he will automatically have a memory flashback of another android he met in ‘From the Dead’. Cannot be missed.”), as one narrated event. The announcements are the game’s strings (X0501M.MONORAIL ANNOUNCE01, 02 and 04); the template does not place them, so their order is assumed. The flashback’s words are the landfill android’s line in From the Dead; the key he copied to {{Markus}} is from the wiki’s Jericho (location) and Phileas pages (“Phileas gave Markus a copy of his key to locate Jericho”), which the game shows rather than says. The coat and the removed LED are From the Dead’s ending (PowerPyx, Markus page). Left out: the wiki’s “news about a detective android”, which has no line in the template. nodes.title: The red mural
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform. A man walks past on his phone: “Hey. Yeah, I’m good. How about you? … I know! It’s crazy, right? Sure, I’ll talk to you later.” A homeless man stops you: “Hey, mister, can you spare some change?..” Two passengers are talking: “I heard that android boyband is going to win some music prize.” “God, they are so creepy.” “My kids don’t listen to anything else.” To your left as you came off the train, a large red mural covers the wall: a figure with a halo and, on its chest inside a red circle, a small mark, a square with an arrowhead above and below it and a bar on either side. Nobody else on the platform looks at it twice. You scan the mark, and the key in your memory decodes it: it is a sign left for androids, and it shows you what the next sign looks like.
facts: The way to {{Jericho}} is a trail of marks hidden in murals and painted signs. Only an android carrying the key can decode them, and each one shows what the next looks like.

nodes.title: A magazine on the bench
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform at {{Ferndale}} Station, before the escalators down to the street. Someone has left a digital magazine on a bench; you can swipe from one cover story to the next.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android on the Run!
facts: Residents of a {{Detroit}} suburb watched a chase after a police manhunt, with roadblocks and dozens of police interviews, flushed out a fugitive. The rogue AX400 model is thought to be suffering from an extremely rare malfunction and took extreme measures to avoid the police, even dashing across a busy highway. Eyewitness statements are inconclusive, there is no official report, and no {{CyberLife}} spokesperson was available for comment.

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer
facts: {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a quantum supercomputer capable of “exaflops”, a billion billion operations per second. It will calculate the probability of mass-extinction events, such as aggressive alien invasions or global disasters like meteors or superviruses, so that humanity can anticipate and prepare for them.

media.title: Tech Addict: Android Astronauts to Explore Io
facts: NASA has launched a crew of five androids on a three-year journey to Io, one of Jupiter’s moons: the first all-machine crew. NASA’s director calls androids an extraordinary asset for the conquest of space, because cosmic radiation destroys human DNA. No return journey is planned; the androids will work on Io for several months before the extreme conditions destroy them.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s three magazine nodes, READ “ON THE RUN”, READ “FORTUNE TELLER” and READ “ANDROID ASTRONAUTS”: covers of one magazine on a bench on the platform (wiki: “on a bench right after Markus gets off the train”; PowerPyx: “before going down the escalator”, “Swipe right to change cover topics”). Android Astronauts to Explore Io (Tech Addict #13) is always there. Android on the Run! (Detroit Today #32) appears only if Kara and Alice were pursued by Connor in On the Run (wiki); CyberLife’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer (Tech Addict #15) appears otherwise. The pursuit is read from On the Run’s flag (`chase`), set whenever the highway chase began, including when it ended with Kara and Alice dead on the highway; a PowerPyx reader’s unconfirmed list puts that case and KARA & ALICE VANISHED under Fortune Teller, but the wiki’s condition is the pursuit itself. Article facts are condensed from the wiki’s magazine pages; NASA’s director, CyberLife’s Director of Futurology and the suburb (Camden) are left unnamed. Corrected from the earlier version of this scene: the article mentions no child, the “extremely rare malfunction” is not a CyberLife statement (no spokesperson was available), and the chapter is in daylight (04:30 PM), not at night. No public-opinion effect: no source gives one.
